# Hectare One — Firmware 1.2.3

# What the Hectare One system does

The seeding control system with the Hectare One panel is made by Agriwelt. It watches sowing and the application of dry and liquid fertilizer on mounted and trailed implements — seed drills, planters, cultivators — and it drives the dispensers and the pump so that the set rate is actually applied.

![The Hectare One panel: the operator's single point of contact with the system.](figures/hw/display)

The panel sits in the cab. Everything else is on the implement: one seed sensor per section, and whatever the machine needs besides — see [What is supplied](whats-supplied.md).

## Seed

- Applies seed to the rate the operator sets, through the dispenser electric motors — on row-crop planters and on grain drills.
- Watches the actual sowing against that rate and reports a section that falls behind.
- Reports a blocked or empty tube **by its number**.
- Counts seeds, **doubles and skips** — on row-crop planters.
- Accepts a section shut-off signal from a third-party navigation system.

![Seed sensor for round seed pipes, 25–35 mm.](figures/hw/seed-sensor)

## Dry and liquid fertilizer

- Applies liquid fertilizer to the rate through the electric pump.
- Watches dry and liquid lines and reports a section that falls behind or blocks, by number.

## The machine around the product

- Hopper level, dispenser shaft rotation, fan speed, air pressure or vacuum, travel speed — each against its own limits.
- The sensors of an autonomous fan-drive engine: oil pressure, battery charge, ignition, fuel level, air filter.
- Working or transport position of the implement.

## Tramline

- Creates the tramline with actuators or by stopping dispenser motors.
- Advances the bout by itself from the marker sensors.
- Keeps watching the sections that are shut off, so that a section leaking into the tramline is still reported.

## Records

- Treated area, separated into what was sown and what was lost to skips.
- Detailed statistics of the run, and reports written to the memory card.
- Firmware of the devices in the system, updated from the same card.

> **NOTE**
>
> The system applies **one product in the “Precise” mode** (seeds per metre), **up to four products by mass** (kilograms per hectare) and **one liquid product** (litres per hectare).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [The panel and its seven buttons](front-panel.md) · [Quick start](quick-start.md) · [Terms](terms.md)


# What is supplied

**The minimum system is the Hectare One panel and the seed sensors** — one sensor per section. Agriwelt seed sensors have their own controller and are connected to the panel directly.

![The Hectare One panel.](figures/hw/display)

Each section of the implement gets its own seed sensor.

![Seed sensor for round seed pipes, 25–35 mm.](figures/hw/seed-sensor)

## Optional devices

Everything else is optional. What a machine carries is written into the panel's [profile](profile.md).

| **Device** | **How many** | **What it is for** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pressure sensor | Up to three | Positive pressure or vacuum. |
| HUB8 input device | As needed | Sensors of the “open collector” kind — speed, hopper, fan, dispenser, work position, markers, Wilger flow meters. |
| Dispenser electric motors | With their controller | Applying seed or dry fertilizer to the rate. |
| Tramline actuators | Up to four | Shutting sections off for the tramline. |
| Electric pump controller | One | Liquid fertilizer — UAN, micro-fertilizers and the like. |

The inductive sensor below serves two jobs: it measures the travel speed, and it watches that a dispenser shaft is turning.

![Inductive sensor for speed and for dispenser shaft rotation.](figures/hw/inductive-sensor)

The HUB8 takes sensors that have no controller of their own and reports each of them to the panel as if it were a device.

![HUB8, the eight-channel input device for contact sensors.](figures/hw/hub8)

One controller design drives the dispenser motors and the liquid fertilizer pump. That is why a machine cannot have a pump without also having the controller a motor would use.

![The electric motor controller; the same unit drives the liquid fertilizer pump.](figures/hw/motor-controller)

> **NOTE**
>
> The panel also works with seed sensors made by **DICKEY-John, Kuhn, Gaspardo** and others.

## Cables

The panel takes its power through its own supply cable.

![Power supply cable of the Hectare panels.](figures/hw/power-cable)

A HUB8 is joined to the system by a 4-pin Amphenol network cable.

![HUB8 network connection cable, Amphenol, 4-pin.](figures/hw/hub8-network-cable)

The sensors plug into the HUB8 through a harness.

![HUB8 sensor connection harness.](figures/hw/hub8-harness)

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [What the system does](overview.md) · [Terms](terms.md#devices)


# Safety

Knowing these rules is the precondition for working with the system safely and without interruption. This manual is part of the delivery: keep it on the machine or in the tractor cab.

## The panel drives machinery

The panel is not only an indicator. The dispenser electric motors, the liquid fertilizer pump and the tramline actuators are started by commands from the panel, and several of those commands work **while the machine is standing still**.

> **WARNING**
>
> **Machinery starts while the machine stands still.** Three things turn the metering shafts at a standstill: **“Fill the disks with seeds”** in the main menu, and **“Fill the rotor cells”** and **“Calibration”** in the mass calibration of an electric motor. On a motor with a calibration button wired to its controller, that button starts the shaft from the machine itself, out of sight of the cab. Before you use any of them, make sure nobody is near the metering units, the dispenser shafts, the fan or the tramline actuators. Filling the disks turns every disk at once, for up to about twenty seconds per motor.

**Speed imitation makes the machine meter product without moving.** With imitation switched on, the panel calculates as if the machine were driving and drives the dispenser motors and the pump accordingly. Switch imitation off before you leave the cab.

**Before you approach the implement,** stop the machine, switch the tractor ignition off and take the key with you. Do not rely on what the panel shows: a device whose control has been switched off reports nothing about its state.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Above the Operator access level the panel shows no alarm messages.** A blocked tube, an empty hopper or a failed section is not reported. Return to **Operator** before working, or switch the panel off and on. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).

## The operator's workplace

The system is operated by **one person, from the driver's seat of the tractor**. Do not operate the panel from outside the cab while the tractor is able to move or while anyone is near the implement.

## Intended use

The system is intended **solely** as a monitoring and control device for sowing and for the application of dry and liquid fertilizer on agricultural machines — mounted and trailed seed drills, planters and cultivators. Following every instruction in this manual is part of intended use. Any other use is not intended use; the manufacturer is not liable for damage arising from it, and the risk is borne by the user alone.

Besides this manual, observe the national safety and environmental rules where the machine is worked, and the safety instructions of the implement and of the tractor.

## Handling the panel

- Do not subject the panel to impact or heavy vibration, and do not drop it.
- Do not touch the screen with sharp objects; they damage the touch surface.
- **Do not open the housing.** It is sealed and carries a pressure equaliser; opening it destroys the seal. Repairs are made by Agriwelt service only.
- Keep the harness connector, the GPS antenna connector and the memory card slot closed and clean when nothing is plugged in.
- Clean with a damp cloth — no solvents, no pressure washer.
- Connect the panel only to a supply that meets the parameters in the device passport. Reversed polarity or a voltage outside the permitted range damages the electronics.
- Disconnect the panel before electric welding on the tractor or the implement.

## Warranty and liability

The general terms of sale and delivery of Agriwelt GmbH apply. Claims for warranty and for damage to persons or property are not accepted where the cause is use other than as intended; improper installation, commissioning or operation; disregard of this manual on commissioning, operation and maintenance; or unauthorised modification of the equipment.

## Signal words in this manual

| **Signal word** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| **DANGER** | An immediate threat with a high degree of risk. Ignoring it leads to death or the severest injuries. |
| **WARNING** | A possible threat with a medium degree of risk. Ignoring it can lead to death or severe injuries. |
| **CAUTION** | A threat with a low degree of risk. Ignoring it can lead to minor or moderate injuries. |
| **IMPORTANT** | No threat to people. Ignoring it damages equipment or costs work that has to be done again. |
| **NOTE** | Information that helps you get more out of the system. |
| **TIP** | A shortcut or a better way of doing something. |
| **SEE ALSO** | A pointer to the topic where the subject is described in full. Not a safety instruction. |


# The panel and its seven buttons

The Hectare One is operated with seven backlit buttons under the screen and with touches on the screen itself. Everything can be done with the buttons alone — with gloves on, on a rough field.

::: {.anatomy fig="one-panel-front"}
1. **Screen.** 800 × 480 colour screen with a touch surface. Shown here: the [home screen](home-screen.md).
2. **“HOME”.** Moves between the working screens. Held down on the home screen, it locks and unlocks product application.
3. **“MINUS”.** Decreases the selected value.
4. **“UP”.** Moves the selection to the previous item of a menu.
5. **“MENU”.** Opens the main menu from the home screen. In a menu it enters the selected item; in a dialogue it confirms.
6. **“DOWN”.** Moves the selection to the next item of a menu.
7. **“PLUS”.** Increases the selected value.
8. **“BACK”.** Leaves a menu or a screen; in a dialogue it cancels. On the home screen it opens the [tramline bout menu](next-tramline-bout.md).

The front of the panel. The buttons are always in this order.
:::

> **TIP**
>
> **The backlight tells you which buttons work.** The panel lights only the buttons that do something on the screen you are looking at; a dark button does nothing there. On the [number pad](interface-basics.md#entering-numbers) **“MENU”** lights green — accept — and **“BACK”** red — cancel.

What each button does on each screen is listed in [Buttons and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md).

## The back of the panel

![The back: mounting plate with ball joint, harness connector, GPS antenna connector and microSD slot.](figures/one-panel-back)

There are no controls on the back. One harness connector of up to fourteen contacts carries everything to the panel. The two raised round caps are the GPS antenna connector and the dust-protected slot of the microSD card; the small opening is the pressure equaliser of the sealed housing. The ball joint lets you turn and tilt the panel freely on a flat surface in the cab. For mounting on a tube, an additional bracket is available.


# Switching on

After the power is switched on, a splash screen with the logo appears. It stays until the panel has found every device connected to it — a few seconds — and then the [home screen](home-screen.md) opens.

> **NOTE**
>
> **If the splash screen stays much longer than usual,** the panel is waiting for a device that does not answer. Nothing is broken yet — but look at the alarms as soon as the home screen appears. See [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## What state the panel starts in

- **Access level: Operator.** The panel starts at the Operator level after every power-on, whatever level was set before. Switching off and on is therefore also the quickest way back to Operator — the only level at which alarm windows are shown. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).
- **The ordinary home screen.** Even on a machine without seed sensors the panel starts on the ordinary home screen; the [second home screen](second-home-screen.md) is opened by hand.

## Switching off

The statistics are written every five minutes and when the machine stops. **Switch the panel off only after you have stopped moving** — otherwise the last stretch of work is lost from the [statistics](statistics-screen.md).


# Menus, context menus, number pad and windows

Everything on the panel happens through five things: the **working screens**, the **main menu**, the **context menu** of a device, the **number pad** and the **windows** that ask or tell you something. The working screens have their own topic: [Working screens](working-screens.md).

## The main menu

Press **“MENU”** on the home screen, or tap the screen with two fingers. The main menu opens over the home screen.

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-main"}
1. **Selected item.** Black text on a light blue band. **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** move the band; **“MENU”** enters the item. Here **“Fill the disks with seeds”** — see [Fill the disks](fill-the-disks.md).
2. **“Settings”.** The settings of the system and of the machine. See [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md).
3. **Arrow head.** The item opens another menu.
4. **“Service”.** Commissioning and service items. See [Service menu](service-menu.md).
5. **“Information”.** Opens the screen with the information about the system.

The main menu of a planter with dispenser motors in the “Precise” mode, standing still.
:::

In any menu, an item is read by what stands on its right:

| **What you see on the right** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| An arrow head | The item opens another menu. Press **“MENU”**. |
| A value between **-** and **+** | Change it with **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”**, right there in the list. |
| A value between **-[** and **]+** | **“PLUS”** or **“MINUS”** opens the number pad. |
| Nothing | The item performs an action. Press **“MENU”**. |

![A menu page with values: the year is edited on the number pad, the other values in the list.](figures/menu-datetime)

**“BACK”** leaves a menu and returns one level up.

## The context menu of a device

Every sensor, motor and indicator on the home screen has its own menu. **Touch and hold the device** — its icon or its column on the diagram — and its context menu opens. On the Motors screen and on the second home screen the same works for a motor tile.

![The context menu of a seed sensor: information, control on or off, and the parameters of the sensor.](figures/one-ctx-seed-sensor)

The first item, **“Information”**, opens the [status screen](sensor-status-screen.md) of the device. The second switches its control: **“Disable control”** or **“Enable control”** — see [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md). Below them stand the parameters; which ones you see depends on the access level ([Access levels](access-levels.md)).

## Entering numbers

When a value is written between square brackets, changing it opens the number pad.

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-keypad"}
1. **Name of the parameter.** Here **“Width, cm”**.
2. **Value.** What you have typed so far.
3. **Backspace.** Deletes the last digit. Touch and hold it to clear the whole value.
4. **Digits.** **1** to **9** and **0**.
5. **Decimal point and minus.** A touch adds the point; touch and hold switches the minus sign, where a negative value is allowed.
6. **Zero.**
7. **“OK”.** Accepts the value. **“MENU”** does the same.

The number pad. **“BACK”**, or a touch outside the pad, leaves without changing anything.
:::

A value outside the permitted range is not taken as typed: the panel sets the nearest limit instead.

## Windows that ask, and windows that tell

Every window has the same shape: one box in the middle of the screen, a **coloured strip** along its top with a word in it, the message under the strip, and the buttons — if any — along the bottom. **Read the strip first:**

| **Strip** | **What kind of window** | **How it closes** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Yellow, “Confirmation”** | The panel asks. Nothing happens until you answer. | Touch **“Yes”** (green) or **“No”** (red). **“PLUS”** answers yes, **“MINUS”** no, **“BACK”** cancels. |
| **Blue, “Information”** | The panel tells you what happened. | Some close by themselves; others close with a touch, **“PLUS”** or **“BACK”**. |
| **Red, “FAILURE!”** | An alarm. | See below. |

![A confirmation window: the yellow strip, the question, Yes and No.](figures/question-zero-readings)

The information window below closes by itself.

![An information window: the blue strip, the word Information, the message Done.](figures/info-done)

## Alarm windows

An alarm window says **what happened**, **on what kind of device**, and **which devices** — their numbers are listed when several identical sensors report the same fault at once. While it is open, the panel beeps.

| **What you do** | **What happens** |
| --- | --- |
| Touch **“Close”** in the window, or press **“HOME”** | This alarm closes. The next one in the queue appears. |
| Hold **“HOME”** | The window closes and the panel returns to the home screen. |

The other six buttons are dark and do nothing while an alarm window is open.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Closing the window stops the sound, not the fault.** Alarms arrive one at a time and are closed one at a time. What each alarm means is in [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).


# Quick start — getting ready and moving off

Your machine may not have every step — skip what it does not have.

## Before the field

::: steps
1. **Calibrate the speed sensor.** Area, rates and deviations are all calculated from the speed; a wrong speed makes every other figure wrong. **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Speed calibration”**, at **Agronomist** level. See [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md).

2. **Calibrate the metering rollers** — on grain drills, and on planters whose fertilizer dispenser is driven by an electric motor. From the context menu of each dispenser or motor, at **Operator** level, standing still. See [Mass calibration of a motor](calibrate-motor-weight.md).

3. **Check the tramline rhythm**, if the machine makes tramlines. See [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).

4. **Check the sensor parameters** — the list is below.

5. **Check each section**: is it under control, does it apply product. See [Four states of a section](section-states.md#the-four-states-of-a-section).

6. **Choose the field** on the Statistics screen. For a new field, erase its statistics first. See [Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md#the-menu-of-the-screen).

7. **Set the rates** — seeding, dry fertilizer, liquid fertilizer. See [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).

8. **Check the access level.** It must be **Operator**.
:::

Steps 1 and 2 are not at the same level. **“Seeding machine parameters”** and the speed calibration under it are **Agronomist**; the mass calibrations in the context menus are **Operator**. The usual order: raise the level to Agronomist ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)), do step 1, drop back to Operator, do the rest.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Step 8 is the one that ruins a day.** From Agronomist level upwards the panel suppresses **every alarm but one**: a blocked tube is not reported. The one that still comes through is **“User is Agronomist! Alarms will not be shown!”** — raised **once**, when seeding starts at that level. Dropping back to Operator raises the suppressed alarms again. Check the level before every start, not once a season.

### Sensor parameters to check

- **Speed sensor** — “Min speed, km/h”, “Max speed, km/h”.
- **Dispenser sensor** — “Period, s”, for each sensor.
- **Fan sensor** — “Minimum, rpm”, “Maximum, rpm”, for each sensor.
- **Pressure sensor** — “Minimum, Pa”, “Maximum, Pa”, for each sensor.
- **Liquid fertilizer pump** — “Pulses per liter”, “Max pressure, Bar”.
- **Seed and dry fertilizer sensors** — “Fraction”, “Correction”, “Recalculation,m” or “Recalculation,sec”; in the “Precise” or “Hybrid” mode also “Rate error,%”.
- **Liquid fertilizer sensors** — “Rate error,%” and, without a pump in the profile, “Pulses per liter”. Wilger flow meters: **red 8900**, **green 15500**, **blue 3400** pulses per liter.
- **Electric motors, “Precise” mode** — “Holes in disk”, for any motor in the group.
- **Electric motors, mass dosing** — for each motor, “Weight, gr” divided by “Rotations” against the roller specification. The mass calibration fills both in.

Most parameters are set **per sensor**. In the seed, dry fertilizer and liquid fertilizer sensor groups and in both motor groups, most parameters are common to the whole group — except sensor control and product application, which stay individual. Details: [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

## Moving off

::: steps
1. Put the implement into the **working** position.

2. **Planters with dispenser motors:** fill the disks — main menu, **“Fill the disks with seeds”**. Without it the first metres of every row are empty. See [Fill the disks](fill-the-disks.md).

3. **Grain drills:** nothing to start. The metering motors begin turning by themselves as soon as the product application control starts — the moment you move off. Move off briskly all the same: the rotor cells have to fill before the first metres are sown at the target rate.

4. Drive.
:::

> **WARNING**
>
> **Filling the disks and starting the motors turn machinery while the machine stands still.** Make sure nobody is near the metering units, the dispenser shafts or the fan.

**When the control starts.** The manual lock must be **off** ([Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md)). If a work position sensor is fitted and switched on, the control begins once you move with the implement lowered; without such a sensor, as soon as you move. The alarms start a few seconds later — the delay is **“Settings”** → **“Alarm delay”**, 2 to 20 seconds.

| **Sound** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| One short beep | The panel sees the machine seeding. From now on the sections are watched. |
| Three short beeps | The seeding has stopped — at the headland, or the columns have sunk under the control line. |

On grain drills in the “Flow” or “Hybrid” mode, let the panel find the alarm level itself: [Set the alarm level automatically](set-the-alarm-level.md).

## While working

Watch four things: the **speed** against the tractor, the **fan and the pressure** inside their range, the **actual rate** against the target, and that no sensor is alarming. The [Table screen](table-screen.md) shows how each section is doing right now; the [Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md) how the whole field has gone.

If the speed sensor fails, see [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md).


# Check the system after installation

Run this check once, when the panel and the devices are mounted and connected. Each step says what to do and what the screen must show. If a step does not give the result, the last column of the [table at the end](#if-a-step-fails) says where to go.

Your machine may not have every device — skip the steps for what it does not have. Stay at the **Operator** level: alarm windows are shown only there ([Access levels](access-levels.md)).

> **WARNING**
>
> **Keep clear of the fan, the dispenser shafts and the metering units while the machine is being tested.** Switch the drives off before you reach into a seed tube.

## The check

::: steps
1. **Check the profile and the devices.** Switch the panel on and wait for the home screen. There must be no **“Connection lost”** alarm, no white indicator with an exclamation mark and no red indicator with an **X**. Check the profile against the machine: the devices and the number of each ([The profile](profile.md)). Then open the status screen of every sensor ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)) and step through them with **“PLUS”**. Every sensor shows **“Link:”** **“Normal”**; every seed sensor shows **Status:** **Working**. See [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

   A white indicator is correct only for a device that is not in your delivery ([The profile](profile.md)).

2. **Check that every seed sensor sits in its own row.** Open the Table screen with **“HOME”** and open the table with the seed counters ([The Table screen](table-screen.md)). It shows the number of seeds; read the count there, not on the view with seeds per metre, which shows values only while the machine moves. Zero the readings ([Zero the readings](zero-the-readings.md)). Drop a few seeds by hand through the seed tube of row 1; instead of seeds you may pass any small object, for example a long cable tie, through the seed tube several times — each pass is counted. Only the line of section 1 must react. Do the same with row 2, then with every other row in turn. A sensor that reacts in another row is connected in the wrong order — call your installation partner or the service support.

   ![The seed counter table of an eight-row planter: seeds per section, deviation bars, total.](figures/one-table-counters)

3. **Check the counting.** Only if your Table screen has the seed counter table. Zero the readings again. Drop a known number of seeds, for example 20, through one tube. Read the figure of that section on the seed counter table, which shows the number of seeds. On a precision planter it matches the number you dropped to within one seed, provided the **“Fraction”** of the seed sensors is set for the size of the seed. If the figure is clearly higher — up to twice the number — the fraction is set too small for this seed: a large seed, for example maize, is then counted as two; set the fraction by the table in [Seed and fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md). If the two differ in another way, write both numbers down and give them to the support ([Before you contact support](before-you-contact-us.md)).

4. **Check the work position sensor.** Only if the machine has one. Raise the implement, then lower it. The status screen of the sensor must change between **Position: Transporting** and **Position: Working**. If it shows the opposite, the setting **“Transporting position signal”** of the sensor is the wrong way round ([Hopper, implement position and engine sensors](hopper-position-engine-sensors.md)).

5. **Check the speed.** Drive. The speed field on the home screen must show a number in white. **XX.X** in red means the input device of the speed sensor does not answer. A yellow figure alternating with **“IMITATION”** means the speed is simulated, not measured. **“SLOWER”** and **“FASTER”** only say that you are outside the permitted range ([Indicators](indicators.md)). If the figure does not match the real speed, calibrate the sensor ([Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md)). If the sensor fails, see [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md).

6. **Check the other sensors the machine has.** One short check each:

   - **Hopper sensor.** Its status screen shows **Pin:** and the level, **“0”** or **“1”**. With the hopper filled the panel must not raise **“Hopper empty”** ([Hopper empty](alarms-hopper.md)).
   - **Fan sensor.** With the fan running, its status screen shows **F=** in Hz and no alarm **“Low speed of rotation”** or **“High speed of rotation”** ([Fan sensor](fan-sensor.md)).
   - **Pressure sensor.** With the fan running, its status screen shows **P=** in kPa and no alarm **“High pressure”** or **“Low pressure”** ([Pressure sensor](pressure-sensor.md)).
   - **Dispenser shaft sensor.** Turn the shaft. Its status screen shows **F=** in Hz and no alarm **“No rotation”** ([Dispenser sensor](dispenser-sensor.md)).
   - **Marker sensors.** Each shows **“Link:”** **“Normal”** on its status screen ([Marker sensors](marker-sensors.md)).
   - **Tramline actuator.** Its status screen shows **Status:** **Pulled in**, **Pulled out** or **Working** — not **Unknown** ([Tramline actuator](tramline-actuator.md)).

7. **Record the result.**
   - **The firmware version.** Press **“MENU”** on the home screen and choose **“Information”** in the main menu. The window shows the firmware version. Write it down.
   - Write down the date, the machine and the number of rows.
   - Take a photo of the status screen of a sensor, or of the sensors one after another, showing **“Link:”** **“Normal”**.

   Keep the notes and the photos. You need them if you must contact the support ([Before you contact support](before-you-contact-us.md)).
:::

## If a step fails {#if-a-step-fails}

| Step | What you see | Where to go |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **“Connection lost”** or **“No connection”** | [Any device: connection lost or wrong device type](alarms-any-device.md) |
| 1 | **“Wrong device type!”** | [Any device: connection lost or wrong device type](alarms-any-device.md) |
| 1 | White indicator for a device you have | [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md) |
| 1 | **“Clogged”**, **“Light struck”**, **“Broken”** | [Seed or fertilizer sensor clogged, light-struck or broken](alarms-sensor-state.md) |
| 1 | Device missing from the profile | [The profile](profile.md) |
| 2, 3 | Wrong row reacts, or the count differs | [Before you contact support](before-you-contact-us.md) |
| 4 | Position does not change, or is reversed | [Hopper, implement position and engine sensors](hopper-position-engine-sensors.md) |
| 5 | No speed, or a wrong speed | [Speed sensor alarms](alarms-speed-sensor.md), [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md), [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md) |
| 6 | Hopper, fan, pressure, dispenser | [Hopper empty](alarms-hopper.md), [Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms](alarms-rotation.md), [Air pressure too high or too low](alarms-pressure.md) |


# About the pictures in this manual

The screens in this manual are real frames from a Hectare One panel, firmware 1.2.3, shot on a test bench instead of a machine in the field. A few things on them belong to the bench. Your panel shows the same screens without them.

| **What you see in a picture** | **Why it is there** | **What your panel shows instead** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A blue **0:00** in the top right corner, or the word **TRIAL** | The bench panel runs on a trial licence. While a trial is active, the clock slot cycles between the time left, the word **TRIAL** and blank. | The time of day. See [Clock](indicators.md#clock). |
| **IMITAT** in yellow in the clock slot | The bench runs in an imitation mode. | The time of day. |
| A yellow speed figure, or **IMITATION** in the speed field | The speed is simulated, not measured — there is no wheel turning on a bench. | The measured speed in white. See [Speed](indicators.md#speed). |
| Columns that move although the machine stands still | The seed flow is imitated by the sensors on the bench. | Columns that move only while seeding. |
| Red hoppers, a red oil can or battery | The bench has no product and no engine. | Green icons while everything is in order. |
| A red **A** box at the lower right of the home screen | Actuators named in the bench profile are not physically fitted, so the panel reports them as faulty. | Nothing — the box is not shown while every actuator is in order. See [Actuator failure](indicators.md#actuator-failure). |
| A red **×** in place of an icon | A device named in the bench profile is not connected. | The icon of the device. |
| Zeros on the Statistics screen | The bench statistics were empty when the frame was taken. | Your figures. |

Animated pictures are series of frames taken from the panel about seven seconds apart. They show how the screen changes while seeding, not how fast.

> **NOTE**
>
> Some window shapes changed in September 2026: question, information and alarm windows were brought to one shape with a coloured strip across the top. Pictures in this manual show the new shape.


# The home screen

The home screen is the main working screen. It shows the diagrams of the section control sensors, the state indicators of the devices and the key figures of the work. What it shows follows the [profile](profile.md): every group of sensors and devices entered there gets its tiles, its columns, its rate field.

## A grain drill with seed and fertilizer

::: {.anatomy fig="one-home-m1"}
1. **Travel speed.** In km/h. Messages about the speed replace the figure. [Speed](indicators.md#speed)
2. **Hoppers.** One icon per hopper sensor, numbered. Red — the level is below the sensor. [Hopper](indicators.md#hopper)
3. **Metering units.** Rotation of the dispenser shafts; the icon turns while the shaft turns. [Metering unit](indicators.md#metering-unit)
4. **Engine sensors.** Oil pressure, battery charge and ignition of the fan-drive engine. [Engine sensors](indicators.md#engine-sensors)
5. **Clock.** The time of day; the slot also carries messages. [Clock](indicators.md#clock)
6. **Memory card.** Shown while a microSD card is in the slot. [Memory card](indicators.md#memory-card)
7. **Fan.** The fan icon and its speed in rpm. [Fan](indicators.md#fan)
8. **Markers.** Which marker arm is down. [Markers](indicators.md#markers)
9. **Tramline bout.** The current bout over the number of bouts in the rhythm. [Tramline bout](indicators.md#tramline-bout)
10. **Area.** Hectares treated on the active field. [Area](indicators.md#area)
11. **Product rate by weight.** The rate of product 1, in kg/ha. [Product rate by weight](indicators.md#product-rate-by-weight)
12. **Seed diagram.** One column per seed sensor; the white line is the control line. [The section diagram](section-diagram.md)
13. **Section numbers.** The number of each section, under its column.
14. **Rate field.** Measured rate on top, target below, in seeds per second here. [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md)
15. **Implement position.** Here a red × — the work position sensor does not answer. [Implement position](indicators.md#implement-position)
16. **Fertilizer diagram.** Sections 25 to 36, with their own rate field in fertilizer units per second.
17. **Actuator failure.** At least one motor or tramline actuator is in an alarm state. [Actuator failure](indicators.md#actuator-failure)

A drill with 24 seed rows and 12 fertilizer rows, standing still on the bench: targets set, actual rates zero.
:::

## A planter at work

::: {.anatomy fig="one-home-precise-at-work"}
1. **Travel speed.** Yellow here, because it is simulated on the bench. [Speed](indicators.md#speed)
2. **Hopper.** Green — product above the sensor.
3. **Pressure.** Vacuum or positive pressure in kPa. [Pressure](indicators.md#pressure)
4. **Area.** Hectares treated on the active field.
5. **Population.** The actual seeding rate in thousands of seeds per hectare. [Population](indicators.md#population)
6. **Memory card.**
7. **Section column.** Green — the row sows within its tolerance. [Column colours](section-states.md#column-colours)
8. **Skips bar.** Yellow hatching on the left of a column: the share of skips in that row.
9. **Doubles bar.** Blue hatching on the right of a column: the share of doubles.
10. **Rate line.** The target rate across all rows.
11. **Tolerance ticks.** Upper and lower limit of the permitted deviation, in every column.
12. **Rate field.** Measured seeds per metre on top, target below.
13. **Implement position.** Green — lowered, in work.
14. **Section numbers.**

An eight-row planter in the “Precise” mode, seeding.
:::

What each indicator means in all its states is in [Indicators](indicators.md); the diagram itself — line, ticks, colours — in [The section diagram](section-diagram.md).

## What you can do from the home screen

| **To do this** | **Do this** |
| --- | --- |
| Open the main menu | **“MENU”**, or tap with two fingers |
| Change the target rate | **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md) |
| Lock or unlock product application | Hold **“HOME”** — [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md) |
| Open the tramline bout menu | **“BACK”** — [Next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md) |
| Let the panel set the alarm level | Double tap, while applying — [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md) |
| Open the settings of a device | Touch and hold its icon or column |
| Go to the next working screen | **“HOME”**, or swipe left — [Working screens](working-screens.md) |
| Open the second home screen | Swipe right — [Second home screen](second-home-screen.md) |

All buttons on all screens: [Buttons and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md).


# The section diagram — columns, line and colours

Each column of the diagram is one section — one seed or fertilizer sensor. Its height is the flow through that section. How the rest is drawn depends on the seeding control mode: **“Precise”** (seeds per metre, with skips and doubles) or **“Flow”** (seeds per second against an alarm level).

## “Precise” mode

::: {.anatomy fig="one-diagram-precise"}
1. **Target rate.** Grey, in seeds per metre (**s/m**). This is the figure **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** change.
2. **Measured rate.** White — the average of the rows now.
3. **Tolerance.** The permitted deviation from the target, in per cent.
4. **Rate line.** The target, drawn across all rows.
5. **Upper tick.** The upper limit of the tolerance, in each column.
6. **Lower tick.** The lower limit of the tolerance.
7. **Column.** Green — the row sows within the tolerance.
8. **Skips bar.** Yellow hatching on the left edge of a column. The taller it is, the more skips in that row.
9. **Doubles bar.** Blue hatching on the right edge of a column. The taller it is, the more doubles.
10. **Section number.**

An eight-row planter seeding at about 5 seeds per metre against a target of 4.3. Rows 3, 6 and 7 skip; rows 5 and 7 double.
:::

## “Flow” mode

::: {.anatomy fig="one-home-flow-at-work"}
1. **Alarm level.** Grey, in seeds per second (**s/s**). The level under which a section counts as losing flow. **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** change it.
2. **Measured rate.** White — the average of the rows now.
3. **Control line.** The alarm level, drawn across all rows.
4. **Column above the line.** Green — the row works.
5. **Empty part of a column.** Dark grey above the green: the higher the green reaches, the more flow.
6. **Section numbers.** Fertilizer sections continue after the seed sections.
7. **Fertilizer diagram.** The same, for the fertilizer sensors.
8. **Fertilizer rate field.** Measured on top, alarm level below, in fertilizer per second (**f/s**).

A drill with 24 seed and 12 fertilizer rows, seeding at 12 km/h. Every column stands above its line.
:::

## The line: rows under it are not under control

The line is the boundary of a partial blockage, not a decoration. A column above the line is a row that works; a column that sinks under it is a row that is losing flow — long before it blocks completely.

::: {.anatomy fig="one-home-flow-not-under-control"}
1. **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”.** The rows of this diagram are not watched.
2. **Columns under the line.** Every row delivers less than the level.
3. **Control line.** Dragged above the real flow.
4. **Alarm level.** 18 seeds per second — more than the machine sows.
5. **Measured rate.** 15 seeds per second.

The same drill with a level set too high. Both diagrams have dropped out of control.
:::

Rows under the line are not under control on purpose: the panel refuses to guard a level that was set above what the machine really delivers. Lower the level until the columns stand above the line, or let the panel set it: [Set the alarm level automatically](set-the-alarm-level.md).

Whether the machine is seeding at all, the panel decides by the **share of rows that are seeding** — a sensor setting, 20 % by default. On the headland the rows drop out of control; on the next pass they come back, with or without a work position sensor. The panel says so with sound: **three short beeps** when the seeding stops, **one short beep** when it starts again.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Read the columns against the line, not against each other.** Above the line the section works. Down at the line it does not — whatever the neighbours do.

What every colour and symbol of a column means, and the four states of a section: [Column colours and section states](section-states.md).


# Column colours and the four states of a section

How the diagram is built — rate line, ticks, control line — is in [The section diagram](section-diagram.md). This page lists what a single column can look like.

## Column colours

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| Green column | The row sows normally. |
| Blue column | The row sows **more** than the target allows (“Precise” and “Hybrid”). |
| Yellow column | The row sows **less** than the target allows (“Precise” and “Hybrid”). |
| Background blinking dark red, no column | The row sows almost nothing while the machine is seeding — a blocked or empty tube. |
| White column with **!** | The control of this section is switched off. Nothing about it is watched. |
| Red **×** | The sensor does not answer. |
| Red **?**, column blinking red | A device of the wrong kind answers in place of this sensor. |
| Yellow **?** | The sensor has just received its settings, or it counts seeds but the panel has no speed to judge them by. |
| Grey hatching over the whole column | The section is shut off for the tramline, or its product application is switched off. |
| Green hatching at the bottom of a grey column | A small flow in a shut-off section, still within what is tolerated. |
| Red hatching in a grey column | The shut-off section sows into the tramline. |

## The four states of a section

Each section has two independent switches: whether the panel **watches** it (control), and whether the machine **applies** through it (product application).

| **Control** | **Application** | **What it means** | **What the column shows** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| on | on | Normal work. | The normal column. |
| on | off | Tramline: the row deliberately does not sow, and the panel knows it. | Grey hatching. |
| off | on | The row sows, but nobody is checking it. | White with **!** |
| off | off | The section is out of the work altogether. | White with **!** |

Control is switched in the context menu of the sensor: [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md). **“Product application”** is an item of the same menu, at the Agronomist level; in tramline mode the actuators or motors switch the sections themselves and this item is ignored.


# The home screen on different machines

What the home screen shows follows the [profile](profile.md). The pictures below were taken on one panel, firmware 1.2.3, set up as different machines. Bench artefacts — the blue clock, the yellow speed — are explained in [About the pictures](about-the-pictures.md).

## An eight-row planter, standing still

::: {.anatomy fig="one-home-01-main"}
1. **Travel speed.** Yellow: the speed is simulated, not measured.
2. **Hoppers.** The first green, the second **red** — that hopper reports empty.
3. **Metering units.** Two dispenser shaft sensors.
4. **Fan.** With its speed in rpm beside it.
5. **Area.** Hectares treated on the active field.
6. **Population.** The actual seeding rate in thousands per hectare.
7. **Memory card.** A microSD card is in the slot.
8. **Tolerance.** The permitted deviation in force, written above the diagram.
9. **Tolerance ticks.** Upper and lower limit, in every column.
10. **Rate line.** The target rate.
11. **Section column.** Empty: the machine stands still.
12. **Rate field.** Measured seeds per metre on top, target below.
13. **Manual lock.** The yellow hand: product application is locked by hand. [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md)
14. **Actuator failure.** A fault of the dispenser electric motors. [Motors screen](motors-screen.md)
15. **Section numbers.**

Eight seed sensors, two dispenser electric motors, two hoppers, two dispenser shaft sensors, one fan; “Precise” mode.
:::

The target rates are set, the actual rates are zero. Forty-four seed sensors in two rows of twenty-two, two hoppers, two dosing shafts, a fan, one rate field in seeds per second; the planter icon at the right is green — the machine is in working position.

## At work

The 24-row drill at 12 km/h. The series starts with the columns **below the line** and **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** over both diagrams; then the target is lowered, the columns rise above the line and the rows are under control again.

## A real machine at work

Shot on a machine with 48 seed sensors in two rows, two hoppers, two dispenser shaft sensors and one fan, while sowing. The rate field is selected for editing: its background is lit, the target is white and the measured value grey. Unselected, it is the other way round.

# Indicators of the home screen

Where each indicator sits is shown in [The home screen](home-screen.md). This page says what each one means, state by state.

## How to read any indicator

![](figures/icons/fan.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/fan-red.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/no-connection.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/not-controlled.png){height=40px}

Almost every indicator follows the same rule. Learn it once and you can read an indicator you have never seen.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/fan.png){height=32px} **Green** icon | Normal. The device answers and its value is inside the limits. |
| ![](figures/icons/fan-red.png){height=32px} **Red** icon, blinking | Alarm. The device answers, but the value has left the limits. An alarm window follows after the alarm delay. |
| ![](figures/icons/no-connection.png){height=32px} Icon alternating with a **red ×** | No answer from the device. The value is shown as **XXXX**. |
| ![](figures/icons/not-controlled.png){height=32px} Icon alternating with a **white [!]** | The device is in the profile, but its control is switched off. The value is shown as **!!!!**. |
| Icon alternating with a red **?** | A device of the wrong kind answers in its place. The value is shown as **????**. |
| ![](figures/icons/work-blocked.png){height=32px} **Yellow** icon | Not a fault. A state you have chosen or that needs your attention: implement raised, markers up, ignition off, application locked by hand. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A switched-off indicator is not a quiet one — it is a blind one.** White with **!!!!** means the panel does not watch that device at all. Nothing will be reported about it, however wrong it goes.

## Speed

![The speed field at the top left.](figures/crops/speed)

The travel speed in km/h. Messages about the speed replace the figure and blink about once a second, so that the figure stays readable.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| A number in white, e.g. **10.0** | Normal. |
| **“SLOWER”** on red | You drive faster than the maximum set for the speed sensor. Slow down. |
| **“FASTER”** on red | You drive slower than the minimum. Speed up. |
| **XX.X** in red | No answer from the input device that carries the speed sensor. |
| **????** in red | A device of the wrong kind answers in place of the speed sensor. |
| A yellow number alternating with **“IMITATION”** | The speed is simulated from the setting of the speed sensor, not measured. Nothing that depends on the speed is real. See [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md). |
| **INCREASE IMITATION** / **DECREASE IMITATION** | The simulated speed itself is outside the permitted range. Change the setting, not the travel speed. |
| **Sensor1** / **Sensor2** | One of two speed sensors has failed. |
| **“Settings”** | The minimum and the maximum speed contradict each other. |

**“SLOWER”** and **“FASTER”** are not alarm windows. They stay in the speed field for as long as the speed is wrong, because you have to see them while correcting it. See [Speed sensor alarms](alarms-speed-sensor.md).

## Clock

The clock slot at the top right is shared by several messages.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| The time in white | Normal. |
| **BAT** in red, for about a second in every four | The clock battery is low. The clock still runs; between the flashes the time is shown in red. Have the battery replaced. |
| **XX:XX** in red, blinking | The clock chip does not answer. The panel has no date and time; everything it records carries the wrong one. |
| **IMITAT** in yellow | The imitation mode of the service menu is on. |
| Blue hours:minutes, then **TRIAL**, then blank | A trial period is running; the blue figure is the time left. When the first row has no room for the clock, this loop appears only now and then. |

## Memory card

![](figures/icons/microsd.png){height=40px}

Shows that a microSD card is in the slot. Two states only: the icon is there, or it is not.

## Hopper

![](figures/icons/bunker-full.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/bunker-empty.png){height=40px}

![Two hopper icons; both report an empty hopper.](figures/crops/hoppers)

A **full green** hopper is normal. An **empty red** one means the level has fallen below the sensor: refill. See [Hopper alarms](alarms-hopper.md).

## Metering unit

![](figures/icons/dosator.png){height=40px}

![Two metering-shaft icons.](figures/crops/dispensers)

The rotation of the dispenser shaft. While the shaft turns, the icon **turns** — the fastest way to see that the metering unit really runs. Red means no rotation, or not the speed required. See [Rotation alarms](alarms-rotation.md).

## Fan

![The fan icon with its speed in rpm.](figures/crops/fan)

The fan speed in revolutions per minute. Green is normal; red — above the maximum or below the minimum. The × and the [!] have the usual meaning.

## Pressure

![](figures/icons/pressure.png){height=40px}

The vacuum or the positive air pressure in the distribution system, in kPa. Green is normal; red — above or below the permitted range. See [Pressure alarms](alarms-pressure.md).

## Engine sensors

![](figures/icons/ignition.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/oil.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/battery.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/fuel.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/airfilter.png){height=40px}

![Oil pressure, battery charge and ignition on the home screen.](figures/crops/engine-sensors)

The sensors of the engine that drives the fan.

| **Indicator** | **Green** | **Red or yellow** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oil pressure | Normal | **Red:** the oil pressure has fallen below the permitted level. |
| Battery charge | Normal | **Red:** the battery is not being charged. |
| Ignition | **Green key:** ignition on, the engine sensors are watched | **Yellow key:** ignition off. Not a fault — but the engine is not watched either. |
| Fuel level | Normal | **Red:** little fuel left in the tank. |
| Air filter | Normal | **Red:** the air filter is clogged; clean or replace it. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Oil pressure and battery charge are watched only while the ignition is on.** With the ignition off, their faults are not reported. See [Tractor and engine alarms](alarms-tractor.md).

## Area

![The area treated on the active field.](figures/crops/area)

The area treated on the [active field](statistics-screen.md), in hectares.

## Population

![](figures/icons/seeds.png){height=40px}

In the “Precise” mode: the actual seeding rate in **thousands of seeds per hectare** (**ths/ha**).

## Product rate by weight

![](figures/icons/product.png){height=40px}

![The product rate in kg/ha.](figures/crops/product-rate)

Shown when the dispensers apply products by weight; one indicator per product, with its number. It shows the rate in kg per hectare.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| Icon **green** | Normal. The machine applies what was asked of it. |
| Icon **red**, blinking | The actual rate is outside the permitted deviation from the target. |
| Field lit, figure blinking | The target is being set. Touch and hold the field to type the target on the number pad, or use **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**. |
| Field lit, not blinking | Setting is on, but another rate field is the one being changed. This one shows its target and waits. |

## Dosing by weight is not possible

A **red blinking product icon** at the right edge. The panel has worked out that the target cannot be held at any travel speed: the lowest speed at which the metering rollers can deliver the rate is already at or above the highest.

**What to do.** Check the target rates first — one product asking too much closes the window for all of them. Then check the metering rollers: a roller of another size may be needed. The speed limits the panel calculated are on the **“Information”** screen of the speed sensor. See [Dosing by weight alarms](alarms-dosing-by-weight.md).

## Markers

![](figures/icons/markers.png){height=40px}

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| **Green**, both arms down | Both markers are lowered. |
| **Green**, one arm down | Only that marker is lowered — left or right, as drawn. |
| **Yellow**, both arms up | Both markers are raised. Not a fault; on a machine that changes the tramline bout by the markers, the bout changes now. |

## Implement position

![](figures/icons/work-allowed.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/work-blocked.png){height=40px}

**Green** — lowered, in work. **Yellow** — raised, in transport, not applying.

## Tramline bout

![](figures/icons/tramline.png){height=40px}

Shown only if the tramline is switched on. The large number is the current bout, the small one under it the number of bouts in the rhythm.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| Bout figures, e.g. 1 over 3 | How far you are from the next tramline. |
| Tramline icon **grey** | The bout changes by itself. |
| Tramline icon **yellow** | The bout does not change by itself: automatic change is switched off, or the sensor it depends on is missing, silent or not under control. Change it by hand. |

See [Move to the next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md).

## Manual lock

![](figures/icons/hand.png){height=40px}

A **yellow hand**, blinking, at the right edge: product application is locked by hand. The machine applies nothing, however it moves. Not shown at all while application is allowed. It appears on machines with electric dispenser motors or a liquid fertilizer pump. See [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md).

## Actuator failure

![](figures/icons/actuator-fail.png){height=40px}

![The actuator failure indicator at the lower right.](figures/crops/actuator-failure)

One icon for all electric motors and tramline actuators together. **Not shown at all while everything is in order.**

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| **Red**, blinking | At least one motor or actuator is in an alarm state. |
| Alternating with **white [!]** | The control of at least one actuator is switched off. No fault is known — but that actuator is not watched. |

Which one and why is on the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md).

## Liquid fertilizer pump

Depending on the equipment, the pump has two or three indicators.

| **Indicator** | **What it shows** |
| --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/pump-rate.png){height=32px} **Rate**, l/min | The main indicator. Its context menu holds the pump parameters. |
| ![](figures/icons/pump-load.png){height=32px} **Load**, % | How hard the pump works. It disappears first when the screen has no room for it. |
| ![](figures/icons/pump-pressure.png){height=32px} **Pressure**, bar | Only if the pressure sensor is fitted and switched on in the pump controller settings. |

**Rate.** Besides green, red, × and [!]: a **yellow pump with STOP** — application is locked by hand or the implement is raised, and the pump will not start when the machine moves; a **lit target figure** — there are no section flow sensors in the profile, so the figure is the target, not a measurement.

**Load.** **At 99 % and above it turns yellow**: the pump is at its limit and cannot follow more speed. Drive slower, or the rate falls below the target. **----** blinking red: the controller reports no load figure.

**Pressure.** **Red means the liquid pressure is too high** — reduce the speed, or raise **“Max pressure, Bar”** in the pump controller settings if the line can really take it. **----** blinking red: the pressure sensor is broken or gives no reading. See [Pump controller alarms](alarms-pump-controller.md).


# The second home screen

This screen was made for a **system without seed sensors**: a machine where the seeding rate is held by the dispenser electric motors and the panel monitors the main working units. On such a machine the ordinary home screen would be almost empty.

**Open it** from the home screen with a **swipe to the right**. **Close it** with **“HOME”** or a swipe to the left. It is not part of the circle of working screens, and the panel does not switch to it by itself — even on a machine without seed sensors it starts on the ordinary home screen.

::: {.anatomy fig="one-home-02-alt-home"}
1. **Fan.** The fan and its speed in rpm.
2. **Seed spacing.** In seeds per metre.
3. **Travel speed.** In km/h; yellow while it is simulated. [Speed](indicators.md#speed)
4. **Area.** Hectares treated on the active field.
5. **Settings symbol.** A touch opens the main menu, the same as **“MENU”**.
6. **Red chevrons.** A touch takes the outermost motor on that side **out of** control.
7. **Green chevrons.** A touch takes the next motor towards that side back **into** control.
8. **Target rate.** In thousands of seeds per hectare. Touch and hold it, then swipe up or down to change it.
9. **Motor 1.** Its number and value; the icon alternates with the state sign — here **STOP**, the motor is not running.
10. **Motor 2.** A red × and **XXX** — no connection; the motor is not driven.
11. **Manual lock.** The yellow hand: application is locked by hand. Touch and hold it, or hold **“HOME”**, to lock or unlock.

The second home screen of a machine with two dispenser motors and one fan, standing still.
:::

Each motor icon **alternates**, about once a second, between the picture of the motor and the sign of its state. In the other blink phase the same screen looks like this — the motors are drawn as motor symbols, and the word **“IMITATION”** has replaced the speed figure because the speed is simulated:

![The same screen in the other blink phase.](figures/one-home-03-alt-home-imitation)

## What you can do here

| **To do this** | **Do this** |
| --- | --- |
| Open the main menu | **“MENU”**, or touch the settings symbol |
| Change the seeding rate | Touch and hold the rate, then swipe up or down. It stays within the permitted limits. |
| Take motors out of or into control | Touch the red or green chevrons at either end of the rate strip. Confirm with **“Yes”** if the panel asks. |
| Open the settings of a motor | Touch and hold the motor |
| Lock or unlock product application | Hold **“HOME”**, or touch and hold the hand. A short beep confirms. |
| Return to the home screen | **“HOME”**, or swipe left |

What the motor states mean: [Motors screen](motors-screen.md#reading-a-tile).


# The working screens and how to move between them

The panel has **four working screens in a circle**, and a fifth that stands apart.

| **Screen** | **What it is for** |
| --- | --- |
| [Home screen](home-screen.md) | The diagrams of the sections, the indicators of the devices, the speed, the area and the rates. The panel starts here. |
| [Table](table-screen.md) | The readings of every section in figures, as a list. Several tables, depending on the control mode. |
| [Statistics](statistics-screen.md) | The results of the work by field: area, path, quantities, quality. |
| [Motors](motors-screen.md) | The dispenser electric motors, and the tramline actuators if the machine has them. Present only if the profile holds at least one motor or tramline actuator. |
| [Second home screen](second-home-screen.md) | A home screen for machines **without seed sensors**. Outside the circle. |

The Motors screen was called the “Actuators” screen in earlier documentation. On most machines it shows the dispenser electric motors, so this manual calls it **Motors**.

## The circle

**“HOME”** moves to the next screen, always in the same direction, and returns to the home screen from the last one:

**Home screen → Table → Statistics → Motors → Home screen.**

Without motors and tramline actuators in the profile, there is no Motors screen and Statistics returns straight to the home screen.

## Every way from one screen to another

A swipe has to be a long one, with one finger, across the screen — a short movement is not taken as a transition.

| **From** | **Action** | **To** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home screen | **“HOME”**, or swipe left | Table |
| Home screen | Swipe **right** | Second home screen |
| Table | **“HOME”**, or swipe left | Statistics |
| Table | **“BACK”**, or swipe right | Home screen |
| Statistics | **“HOME”**, or swipe left | Motors (home screen, if the machine has none) |
| Statistics | Swipe right | Table |
| Statistics | **“BACK”** | Home screen |
| Motors | **“HOME”**, **“BACK”**, or swipe left | Home screen |
| Motors | Swipe right | Statistics |
| Second home screen | **“HOME”**, or swipe left | Home screen |

> **NOTE**
>
> **A swipe to the right does not always mean the same.** On the home screen it opens the second home screen. On every other working screen it is the way **back**.

## Buttons or gestures

Almost everything on the working screens can be done with a button **or** with a gesture.

| **Screen** | **What it does** | **Button** | **Gesture** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Home screen | Opens the main menu | **“MENU”** | Tap with **two fingers** |
| Home screen | Sets the alarm level from the real rate | — | **Double tap** with one finger, while applying |
| Home screen | Opens the second home screen | — | Swipe right |
| Table | Scrolls the rows | **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Swipe up or down |
| Table | Previous or next table | **“MINUS”** / **“PLUS”** | Long swipe left or right with **two fingers** |
| Table | Asks whether to zero the readings | **“MENU”** | Tap with **two fingers** |
| Statistics | Scrolls the report | **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Swipe up or down |
| Statistics | Shows another field | **“MINUS”** / **“PLUS”** | Swipe left or right with **two fingers** |
| Statistics | Opens the menu of the screen | **“MENU”** | Tap with **two fingers** |

Two actions on the working screens have no button: the swipe right that opens the second home screen, and the double tap that sets the alarm level. Everything else can be reached from the buttons. The full list per screen: [Buttons and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md).


# The Table screen

The Table screen shows the readings of every section as figures, one line per section. It answers the question the diagram cannot: *which section exactly, and by how much.* Open it from the home screen with **“HOME”**; leave it with **“BACK”**.

## A planter in the “Precise” mode

::: {.anatomy fig="one-table-precise-at-work"}
1. **#.** The number of the section.
2. **sds/m.** Seeds per metre, measured now.
3. **Q.%.** Quality — the share of seeds placed singly, as intended.
4. **Db%.** Doubles — two seeds where one was intended.
5. **Sk%.** Skips — a gap where a seed was intended.
6. **ks/Ha.** The applied rate in thousands of seeds per hectare (in the second table: seeds per metre).
7. **%.** The deviation of this section from the rate that was set.
8. **Table number.** This table and how many there are, between **(−)** and **(+)** — **“MINUS”** and **“PLUS”** switch tables.
9. **Section number on yellow.** Something in this line has drifted towards its limit.
10. **Value on yellow.** The figure that drifted — here the skips of section 7.
11. **Totals.** The same columns for the whole machine.

The first of three tables of an eight-row planter, while seeding.
:::

A value on **yellow** is drifting towards its limit; on **red** it is beyond it. A whole line in **grey** with **!** is a section taken out of control; a line in **red** with **×** is a sensor that does not answer, with **?** a device of the wrong kind.

> **NOTE**
>
> **Read the deviation column first.** A section 20 % below the others has a problem the average will not show — a partly blocked outlet, a worn disk, a sensor that needs cleaning.

## A drill in the “Flow” mode

::: {.anatomy fig="table-1"}
1. **#.** The number of the section.
2. **sds/s.** Seeds per second. Dashes while nothing is counted.
3. **Deviation scale.** From −50 % through 0 to +50 %.
4. **Deviation bar.** How far this section stands from the rate that was set.
5. **%.** The same deviation as a figure.
6. **Table number.** Table 1 of 2 — the second holds the fertilizer sections.
7. **Lowest deviation.** The section furthest below the rate.
8. **Highest deviation.** The section furthest above the rate.
9. **Recalculation interval.** The stretch over which the figures are gathered — **“Recalculation,m”** of the sensors.

The seed table of a drill with 24 seed and 12 fertilizer rows, standing still.
:::

## Which tables your machine has

| **Table** | **Shown when** |
| --- | --- |
| **Seed counters** — seeds per second or per metre, with the deviation bars | Always. |
| **Rate per area** (thousands per hectare) and **rate per distance** (seeds per metre) | Only in the **“Precise”** seeding control mode. |
| **Dry fertilizer** | The machine has fertilizer sensors and the fertilizer control mode is not “Precise”. |
| **Liquid fertilizer** | The machine has liquid fertilizer sensors. |

In the “Precise” mode the planter above has three tables: rate per area (1/3), rate per distance (2/3), and the seed counters (3/3) — the count of seeds each section has sown, beside the deviation bars, with the total for the machine in thousands at the bottom.

![The seed counter table of the eight-row planter: seeds per section, deviation bars, total.](figures/one-table-counters)

## Working with the screen

| **What you want** | **Button** | **Or gesture** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Next or previous table | **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Long swipe left or right with two fingers |
| Scroll the lines | **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Swipe up or down |
| Zero the readings | **“MENU”** | Tap with two fingers |
| Go to Statistics | **“HOME”** | Swipe left |
| Back to the home screen | **“BACK”** | Swipe right |

Zeroing: [Zero the readings](zero-the-readings.md).

## The table while seeding

The lines change with every count; a line that drifts turns yellow.

![The table of the 24-row drill while seeding, seeds and fertilizer.](figures/one-table-live-24-12)

On large machines the rows do not fit on one page: **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** scroll them.

![The table of the 96-row machine while seeding.](figures/one-table-live-48-48)


# The Statistics screen

The Statistics screen is the report of the work: how far you drove, how much you covered, how much you sowed, and how evenly. It is kept **separately for each field** and survives switching off. Open it with **“HOME”** from the Table screen (twice from the home screen); leave it with **“BACK”**.

The report is one long list. Scroll it with **“UP”** and **“DOWN”**, or swipe up and down.

## The head and the work on the field

::: {.anatomy fig="one-stat-precise-head"}
1. **Field number.** The field whose report you see. **“MINUS”** and **“PLUS”** — or a two-finger swipe — show another field.
2. **(A).** This is the active field — the one the panel writes to now.
3. **Date and time.** Today's date and the time of day.
4. **Path.** Distance driven, in km.
5. **Area.** Area covered, in ha.
6. **Operating time.** Hours, minutes and seconds of work.
7. **Movement speed.** The average travel speed.
8. **Started / Ended.** When the work on this field began and ended.
9. **Seeding.** The next block — see below.

The head of the report of an eight-row planter in the “Precise” mode, empty.
:::

## The seeding block

::: {.anatomy fig="one-stat-precise-seeding"}
1. **Seeds sown (x1000).** The total, in thousands of seeds.
2. **Quality.** The share of seeds placed singly, as intended. Judge the work by this number.
3. **Doubles.** Two seeds where one was intended.
4. **Skips.** A gap where a seed was intended.
5. **Not sown.** The share of the run when nothing came out at all.
6. **Actual / Target.** What was applied against what was set.
7. **Population, ths/ha.** In thousands per hectare; the deviation in brackets.
8. **Rate, s/m.** In seeds per metre; the target on the right.
9. **Sown / Not sown / Unknown.** The field split three ways, in hectares.
10. **Bar.** The same split as a coloured bar: green sown, red not sown, grey unknown.
11. **Seed sensors.** The next block — section by section.
:::

**Unknown** is the area driven while the panel could not judge — not a fault, but not proof of work either.

> **NOTE**
>
> **A large deviation is not always a fault of the machine.** Before changing anything on the drill, check that the speed the panel sees matches the real one — a wrong speed moves every rate figure with it.

## Section by section

::: {.anatomy fig="one-stat-precise-sensors"}
1. **Seed sensors.** One block per section follows.
2. **Seed sensor 1.** The section number, and the seeds it counted.
3. **q d s n.** Quality, doubles, skips and not sown for this section.
4. **Sown / not sown / unknown.** The share of each for this section (**s**, **n**, **?**) and the bar.
5. **Population.** Thousands per hectare for this section, with its deviation.
6. **Spacing.** Seeds per metre for this section, with its deviation.
:::

This is where an uneven drill shows itself. A section with a lower quality than the rest, or a longer red part of its bar, points at that row: a blocked outlet, a worn disk, a sensor that needs cleaning.

## Blocks that appear on other machines

| **Block** | **What it holds** |
| --- | --- |
| **Work without alarms control** | The part of the work the panel was **not** watching — driven with the control switched off or locked. |
| **Speed control** | How far and how long you drove outside the permitted speed range. |
| **Fertilizing**, **Liquid fertilizer** | Fertilized / not fertilized / unknown, if the machine applies them. |
| **Product** | For a product applied by weight: the quantity applied, and the actual against the target rate in kg/ha. |

![The report of a drill with a product applied by weight.](figures/one-stat-1-field)

## The menu of the screen

Press **“MENU”**, or tap with two fingers.

![The menu of the Statistics screen.](figures/one-stat-menu)

| **Item** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Select field”** | Makes the field shown the active one — the panel writes to it from now on. Shown only while you look at a field that is not active. A field whose statistics are not empty cannot be selected until its data is erased; the panel says so and asks. |
| **“Statistics”** | Switches the report between **short** and **full**. The short report keeps the totals and drops the per-section detail. |
| **“Mileage”** | Path in km and area in ha over the whole life of the system. These totals cannot be reset. Without a speed sensor, the accumulated running time instead. |
| **“Save to SD-card”** | Writes one field, or all of them, to the memory card. Shown while a card is in the slot. |
| **“Zero statistics”** | Erases the statistics. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The statistics are also erased by something else.** Changing the seeding control mode between “Precise” and the others asks for confirmation and, if you confirm, **erases the statistics of every field**. Save what you need to the memory card first.


# The Motors screen

The Motors screen shows the dispenser electric motors of the machine, one tile each, and the tramline actuators if the machine has any. Look here when a row stops sowing and you want to know whether the motor is the reason.

It exists on any machine whose profile holds **at least one electric motor or one tramline actuator**. Reach it with **“HOME”** from the Statistics screen; leave it with **“HOME”** or **“BACK”**.

::: {.anatomy fig="motors"}
1. **Motor 1, STOP.** Yellow — the motor is serviceable, but product application is not running.
2. **Value of motor 1.** The driven shaft speed in rpm, or seeds per metre in the “Precise” mode.
3. **Motor 2, red ×.** No connection to this motor.
4. **XXX.** No value, because the motor does not answer.

The Motors screen of a machine with two dispenser motors and no tramline actuators.
:::

## Reading a tile

The colour of the symbol is the state. The value beside it is the driven shaft speed in rpm — or, in the **“Precise”** control mode, the seeds per metre measured by the seed sensor of that row.

| **Symbol** | **Value** | **State** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Motor, **green** | the figure | Normal. The motor is under control and driven. |
| **STOP**, yellow | the figure | The motor is serviceable, but **product application is switched off**. Nothing is wrong with it — the system is simply not applying. |
| Motor, **red** | the figure | The motor is in an alarm state. Read the alarm for the reason: [Motor controller alarms](alarms-motor-controller.md). |
| **×**, red | **XXX** | **No connection.** Check the cable and the connector first. |
| **?**, red | **???** | The panel cannot tell what this device is: another kind of device answers in its place, or the controller has stayed in its firmware update mode. |
| **!**, outlined | **!!!** | The motor is **taken out of control** by the operator. It is neither driven nor watched. |

> **NOTE**
>
> **Yellow is not a fault.** A screen full of yellow STOP signs means application is off — at the headland, or locked by hand from the home screen. Red is a fault; yellow is a state you chose.

## Tramline actuators

| **Actuator symbol** | **State** |
| --- | --- |
| Pulled in or pulled out, **green** | The actuator has reached its position. |
| Pulled in or pulled out, **yellow** | The actuator is moving to that position. |
| Alternating between in and out, **yellow** | The panel cannot tell the actuator's position. |
| Blinking **red** | The actuator is in an alarm state: [Tramline alarms](alarms-tramline.md). |
| Blinking **red ×** or **?** | No connection, or a device of the wrong kind. |
| Blinking **white** | The actuator is taken out of control. |

## Working with the screen

| **What you want** | **Button** | **Or gesture** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The settings of one motor | — | Touch and hold its tile |
| Back to the Statistics screen | — | Swipe right |
| Back to the home screen | **“HOME”** or **“BACK”** | Swipe left |

The long press opens the context menu of the motor you pressed. The same menu is reached from the home screen, but here you see every motor of the machine at once and can choose the one that misbehaves. See [Dispenser motor settings](dispenser-motor.md).


# Change the target rate

The rate field at the right of each diagram shows two numbers: **the measured rate on top, the target below it**. In the “Flow” mode the target is the alarm level of the diagram — see [The section diagram](section-diagram.md).

## With the buttons

::: steps
1. On the home screen, press **“PLUS”** or **“MINUS”** once. A rate field is selected and starts to blink; nothing has changed yet.

   ![The rate field at the right selected for editing: lit background, target in white.](figures/one-home-main-norm)

2. Press **“PLUS”** to raise the target or **“MINUS”** to lower it, one step per press.

3. If the machine has more than one rate field — seed and fertilizer, or products by weight — press **“DOWN”** or **“UP”** to move to the next or the previous one.

4. Press **“BACK”** to finish. The field stops blinking and the new target is in force.
:::

## By touch

::: steps
1. Touch and hold the rate field of a diagram. It lights up.

2. Swipe up over the screen to raise the target, down to lower it — one step per swipe.

3. Touch the screen outside the diagrams to finish.
:::

For a **product applied by weight**, touching and holding its kg/ha indicator opens the number pad instead: type the target and touch **“OK”** ([Entering numbers](interface-basics.md#entering-numbers)). On the [second home screen](second-home-screen.md), touch and hold the rate, then swipe.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Columns under the line are not guarded.** If the target is set far above what the machine really delivers, the columns sink under the control line and the panel shows **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”**. On a grain drill, let the panel find the level: [Set the alarm level automatically](set-the-alarm-level.md).


# Lock product application by hand

The manual lock stops **all product application**: the dispenser motors and the pump do not run, however the machine moves. Use it to cross a field already sown, to drive on the road with the implement lowered, or when you work [without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md).

::: steps
1. On the home screen, **hold “HOME”** until the panel beeps once.

2. Check the right edge of the screen. A **yellow hand** blinks there: application is locked.

   ![](figures/icons/hand.png){height=48px}

3. To unlock, hold **“HOME”** again. One short beep; the hand disappears.
:::

On the second home screen the same works with **“HOME”**, or by touching and holding the hand.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The lock is announced by the screen only.** Look for the yellow hand before you start a pass. A locked machine drives a whole field and sows nothing.

## What the lock changes elsewhere

- The motor tiles on the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md) show a yellow **STOP** — serviceable, not applying.
- The pump rate indicator shows a yellow pump with **STOP** ([Liquid fertilizer pump](indicators.md#liquid-fertilizer-pump)).
- The product application control does not start when you move off — the lock must be off for the control to start ([Quick start](quick-start.md#moving-off)).
- The work done while locked is counted in the statistics as **Work without alarms control** ([Statistics](statistics-screen.md)).

The yellow hand is shown on machines with electric dispenser motors or a liquid fertilizer pump.


# Set the alarm level automatically

On a grain drill the seeds arrive too close together to be counted one by one, so the panel guards each row against an **alarm level**: the line on the diagram. Set it too high and every row sinks under the line — **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”**. Set it too low and a half-blocked row goes unnoticed. The panel can set it for you from what the machine really sows.

This works in the **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** modes, for the seed and the dry fertilizer diagrams, and for liquid fertilizer in the “Flow” mode.

::: steps
1. Start seeding at your normal speed, with product flowing through every row.

2. **Double tap** the home screen with one finger.

3. The panel beeps once and lights the rate field: the new alarm level is set from the rate being sown now.

   ![The diagrams with the columns above the line.](figures/one-home-flow-at-work)

4. Check that every column stands above its line.
:::

The double tap works only while product is being applied. Standing still, nothing happens.

> **TIP**
>
