> **Repeat it after a change of seed lot or speed.** The level follows the rate at the moment of the tap. You can also correct it by hand with **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** — see [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).

What the line means and why rows under it are not watched: [The section diagram](section-diagram.md#the-line-rows-under-it-are-not-under-control).


# Take a sensor into or out of control

A sensor **out of control** is not watched: the panel raises no alarm about it, whatever it reports. Take a sensor out of control when its section is out of work on purpose or when the sensor is broken and you must finish the field. Take it back as soon as you can.

## Take a sensor out of control

::: steps
1. On the home screen, **touch and hold** the sensor — its column on the diagram, or its icon. Its context menu opens.

   ![The context menu of a seed sensor.](figures/one-ctx-seed-sensor)

2. Select **“Disable control”** with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and press **“MENU”**, or touch the item.

3. The panel asks **“Are you sure that you want disable control?”**. Touch **“Yes”**, or press **“PLUS”**.

   ![The confirmation before control is switched off.](figures/one-question-disable-control)

4. The column turns white with **!** (an icon alternates with a white [!]). The sensor is no longer watched.
:::

## Take it back into control

Do the same and choose **“Enable control”**. The panel asks **“Are you sure that you want enable control?”**; confirm with **“Yes”**. A seed sensor taken back into control shows a yellow **?** for a few seconds while it receives its settings.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A switched-off sensor is blind, not quiet.** Nothing about it is reported, however wrong it goes.

## When the statistics must be erased

For some sensors the panel first asks to erase the statistics of the active field: it says **“Data for the selected field must be erased!”** and asks again. **“Yes”** erases the statistics of the active field — at the Operator level only after the Agronomist PIN — and changes the control; **“No”** leaves both as they are.

The speed sensor cannot be taken out of control. Motors are taken out of control the same way, from their tile on the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md) or with the chevrons on the [second home screen](second-home-screen.md). What the four combinations of control and product application mean: [The four states of a section](section-states.md#the-four-states-of-a-section).


# Zero the readings of the Table screen

The Table screen keeps counting from the moment its readings were last zeroed. Zero them when you start a new field or a new seed lot, so that the counters and deviations describe only the new work.

::: steps
1. Open the Table screen: **“HOME”** on the home screen.

2. Press **“MENU”**, or tap the screen with two fingers. The panel asks **“Zero readings?”**.

   ![The question before zeroing: Yes in green, No in red.](figures/question-zero-readings)

3. Touch **“Yes”**, or press **“PLUS”**. The counters of every seed, dry fertilizer and liquid fertilizer sensor are set to zero.
:::

**“No”**, **“MINUS”** or **“BACK”** leaves everything as it was.

**Only the counters of the Table screen are zeroed.** The [field statistics](statistics-screen.md) are not touched; they are erased with **“Zero statistics”** in the menu of the Statistics screen.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Zeroing cannot be undone.** Do it when you start something new, not to tidy the screen.


# Fill the disks with seeds

This applies only to planters with seed **dispenser electric motors** in the **“Precise”** control mode. Without motors in the profile, or in another mode, the menu item is not shown.

When the disks are driven by electric motors, they stand empty until the motors run. Drive off with empty disks and the first metres of every row get nothing: each disk has to pick up seeds and carry them round to the drop point first. Filling turns the disks while the machine stands still, so that sowing starts from the first metre.

> **WARNING**
>
> **The disks turn while the machine stands still.** Before you start, make sure nobody is near the metering units, the dispenser shafts or the drive. Every disk starts at once and keeps turning for up to about twenty seconds. From the cab the metering units cannot be seen.

::: steps
1. Stop the machine. The item is shown only while the machine **stands still**.

2. On the home screen, press **“MENU”**. Select **“Fill the disks with seeds”** and press **“MENU”**.

   ![The main menu with Fill the disks with seeds selected.](figures/menu-main)

3. The panel asks **“Are you sure?”**. Touch **“Yes”**, or press **“PLUS”**. **“No”**, **“MINUS”** or **“BACK”** cancels.

   ![The confirmation before the disks turn.](figures/one-fill-01-confirm)

4. Watch the tiles. Each motor turns its disk until the seed sensor of its row registers the first seed. At the end the panel beeps three times and shows **“Operation complete.”**

5. Touch **“Close”**, or press **“BACK”**, to return to the home screen.
:::

To stop before the end, touch **“Cancel”** or press **“BACK”**: the motors stop at once and their control goes back to the seeding logic.

## Reading the screen

::: {.anatomy fig="one-fill-02-screen"}
1. **Green tile.** Done: the seed sensor registered a seed, the disk is filled.
2. **Dark red tile.** Failed: the disk could not be filled. The motor number is bright red.
3. **Reason letters.** Why the tile failed — see the table below. Here **m g**.
4. **“Operation complete.”** Every motor has finished.
5. **“Close”.** Returns to the home screen. While the operation runs, this button reads **“Cancel”**.

The end of the operation on an eight-motor planter: motor 1 filled, motors 2 to 8 failed.
:::

| **Tile** | **State** |
| --- | --- |
| Dark grey | Waiting its turn. Up to eight motors run at the same time; the rest wait. |
| Yellow | Running: the disk is turning. |
| Green | Done. |
| Dark red | Failed. |

Each motor turns its disk at **4 rpm of the driven shaft**. If no seed is registered within **1.25 revolutions — about 19 seconds** — that motor is stopped and marked as failed. A motor already in an alarm state is marked as failed at once.

## Letters on a failed tile

The colour of the letter matters as much as the letter: **red means a fault, white means taken out of control.**

![A failed tile close up.](figures/one-fill-tile-red)

| **Letter** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **m** red | A fault of the dispenser electric motor during the operation. |
| **m** white | The motor is taken out of control and cannot run. |
| **g** red | The seed sensor registered no seed while the disk was turning. |
| **s** red | A fault of the seed sensor during the operation. |
| **s** white | The seed sensor is taken out of control. |

If the **seed sensor** is out of control, the panel cannot check the disk. A serviceable motor still turns it for about one and a quarter turns, so in practice the disk does get filled — but the panel reports that motor as failed, because it never saw a seed.


# Set up the tramline rhythm

A **tramline** is the lane the sprayer will drive in later. You make it now, while sowing, by shutting off one or two sections on certain bouts so that nothing is sown where the sprayer wheels will go. Which bouts those are depends on the width of the drill against the width of the sprayer. That pattern, repeating across the field, is the **rhythm**.

## How a rhythm works — an example

A 6-metre drill and an 18-metre sprayer: every third bout must carry the lane. The rhythm is three bouts long, and actuator 1 shuts its sections off on one of them.

| **Bout** | **Actuator 1** | **What is sown** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | shuts its sections off | All rows except the tramline rows — the lane is made. |
| 2 | open | All rows. |
| 3 | open | All rows. |
| 1 again | shuts off | The next lane, 18 m further. |

The panel counts the bouts and shuts the sections off on the right one. After the last bout it starts again at bout 1.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Get the rhythm wrong and the field looks perfect until the sprayer arrives and has nowhere to drive.** Check the bout count against the sprayer, not against the drill.

## What the panel allows

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Rhythms stored** | **Three.** One is active at a time. Keep the patterns of the machines you work with and switch between them. |
| **Actuators in one rhythm** | **Four.** |
| **Cut-off bouts per actuator** | **Four** different bouts of the same rhythm. |
| **Bouts in a rhythm** | At least one. |

## Setting it up

The tramline items sit under **“Seeding machine parameters”**, which needs the **Agronomist** level: [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

::: steps
1. On the home screen press **“MENU”**, select **“Settings”** and press **“MENU”**.

   ![The main menu.](figures/menu-main)

2. Select **“Seeding machine parameters”** and press **“MENU”**.

   ![The Settings menu; Seeding machine parameters at the bottom.](figures/menu-settings)

3. Select **“Tramline”** and press **“MENU”**.

   ![The Seeding machine parameters menu with the Tramline item.](figures/menu-seeding)

4. Set **“Tramline”** to **“Yes”** with **“PLUS”**. Then select **“Tramline rhythm settings”** and press **“MENU”**.

   ![The Tramline menu.](figures/menu-tramline)

5. On **“Rhythm”**, choose the rhythm number with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**, press **“MENU”** and choose **“Select”**. The word **“Active”** appears beside the number — without it the rhythm is stored but not used.

   ![The rhythm menu: Select, Reset rhythm settings.](figures/one-tramline-rhythm-select)

6. Move down to **“Bouts”** and set the number of bouts in the rhythm.

7. Move to the framed cell under the activation heading and press **“MENU”**. Choose the number of the actuator, then the **bout** on which it must shut its sections off.

8. If the pattern needs it, add more bouts to the same actuator — up to four — with the framed cell at the end of its row, or another actuator with the cell on the empty row below.

9. Press **“BACK”** until the home screen returns. The rhythm is saved; the tramline indicator shows the current bout above and the number of bouts below.

   ![The home screen with the tramline indicator, bout 1 of 1.](figures/one-home-tramline)
:::

Return to the **Operator** level before you work — above it, no alarms are shown.

## The rhythm form

::: {.anatomy fig="one-tramline-rhythm-form"}
1. **Rhythm.** The number of the rhythm; **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** step through the three.
2. **“Active”.** This rhythm is the one in use.
3. **“Bouts”.** The number of bouts in the rhythm.
4. **Activation heading.** **“Tramline actuators activation”** on a machine that makes tramlines with actuators; **“Tramline motors activation”** on one that stops dispenser motors.
5. **Framed cell.** Adds an actuator (or motor) and its cut-off bout.

A new rhythm: one bout, nothing shut off yet.
:::

In the form, **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** move between lines, **“MINUS”** and **“PLUS”** along a line, **“MENU”** opens the selected cell. Moving to the next bout while working: [Move to the next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md).


# Move to the next tramline bout

The tramline indicator on the home screen shows the current bout above and the number of bouts in the rhythm below. The bout can change by itself at every turn, or you change it by hand — both from the **bout menu**, opened with a short press of **“BACK”** on the home screen.

![The bout menu when the bout can change by itself: Auto-switching and Active bout.](figures/one-tramline-bout-menu)

## Automatic change

The panel can change the bout by itself only if something tells it that a bout has ended:

| **On the machine** | **What ends a bout** |
| --- | --- |
| Marker sensors in the profile | At least one marker sensor **under control** and **answering**. The change of the marker position ends the bout. |
| No markers | The **work position sensor**, under control and answering. Raising the implement out of work ends the bout. |
| Neither | Automatic change is impossible. Change the bout by hand. |

On top of that, **“Auto-switching”** must be **“Yes”**, and the machine must actually have been applying and then stopped. All of it together — otherwise the bout stays where it is. When the bout cannot change by itself, the tramline icon on the home screen is **yellow** ([Tramline bout](indicators.md#tramline-bout)).

::: steps
1. On the home screen, press **“BACK”**. The bout menu opens.

2. On **“Auto-switching”**, choose **“Yes”** with **“PLUS”**.

3. Press **“BACK”** to close the menu.
:::

> **NOTE**
>
> **If the bout does not advance at the headland,** check in this order: is **“Auto-switching”** on; is the marker or position sensor under control; does it answer. The first is a setting, the other two are the machine.

## By hand

What the bout menu offers depends on the machine:

- **Without** a sensor that can end a bout, it offers **“Next bout”**. Select it and press **“MENU”**: the bout moves on by one and the menu closes. Do it at every turn.
- **With** such a sensor, it offers **“Auto-switching”** instead. To correct the count — after a missed turn, say — set **“Active bout”** with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**; the new bout takes effect when you close the menu.

**“Active bout”** is in the menu on every machine. Check the indicator on the home screen before you start a pass.

The rhythm itself is set up in [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).


# Set the screen brightness

::: steps
1. On the home screen press **“MENU”**, select **“Settings”** and press **“MENU”**.

2. **“Brightness,%”** is the first item. Change it with **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”**, from 0 to 100 in steps of 10.

   ![The Settings menu with Brightness,% selected and set to AUTO.](figures/menu-settings)

3. Press **“BACK”** to leave the menu. The new brightness stays in force.
:::

**0 means automatic** — the menu shows **“AUTO”**. The panel measures the light in the cab and sets the screen itself: bright in the sun, dim at night. Any other value fixes the screen at that percentage.

The button backlight always follows the screen: when the screen dims, the buttons dim with it.

Everything else in the Settings menu: [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md).


# Work without the speed sensor

**Symptom.** The speed field shows **XX.X** in red, or the speed stays at zero although the machine moves. Without a speed, the panel cannot calculate area, rates or deviations, and the dispenser motors do not know how fast to turn.

**Cause.** The speed sensor or its input device does not answer, or the wheel no longer gives pulses. See [Speed sensor alarms](alarms-speed-sensor.md).

**What to do.** Finish the field on a **simulated speed** and switch the application on and off by hand.

> **WARNING**
>
> **With speed imitation on, the panel drives the dispenser motors and the pump as if the machine were moving** — also while it stands. Switch imitation off before you leave the cab, and lock application whenever you stop.

::: steps
1. On the home screen, touch and hold the speed field. Its context menu opens.

2. Set **“Imitation, km/h”** to the speed you will drive. This item needs the Agronomist level: [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

3. Return to the **Operator** level, so that alarms are shown again.

4. The speed field now shows a yellow figure alternating with **“IMITATION”** ([Speed](indicators.md#speed)).

5. Control the application with the **manual lock**: hold **“HOME”** to stop applying at the headland, hold it again to start on the next pass. While the lock is on, the yellow hand shows at the right edge and the speed reads zero. See [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md).

6. Drive at the speed you set. The rates are right only as long as the real speed matches it.
:::

When the sensor is repaired, set **“Imitation, km/h”** back to 0.

Details of the speed sensor settings: [Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).


# Access levels

Not every setting is open to everyone. The panel has three working access levels. **After every power-on it starts at the lowest one, “Operator”.**

| Level | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| **“Operator”** | Everyday work. Some parameters cannot be changed, and the statistics cannot be reset. |
| **“Agronomist”** | Resetting the statistics, the seeding machine parameters, the product rate error and the other commissioning settings. Needs a PIN. |
| **“Service”** | The profile and the reset-to-defaults items. For the service department. Needs a PIN. |

A fourth level, **“Debug”**, exists above **“Service”**. It is used at manufacture only; see [The Service menu](service-menu.md).

Every settings table in this manual names the level an item needs. An item above your level is not shown in the menu at all.

## Switch the level

The level is changed in the **“Settings”** menu, item **“User”**, and nowhere else — there is no button combination for it. Going **up** a level asks for the PIN; going **down** does not. Step by step, with the screens: [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

The PIN is different for every panel. Take it from the device passport or ask the service support.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **At “Agronomist” and “Service” no alarm windows are shown.** The panel warns about it in a red window — see [User is Agronomist](alarms-access-level.md). Return to **“Operator”** before you work — or switch the panel off and on.

## What happens to the alarms while the level is high

The alarms are not lost while they are hidden — they wait. When you lower the level, the panel drops the ones that have gone away in the meantime and shows the ones that are **still true**, one window after another. After an hour of commissioning at **“Agronomist”**, expect a short run of alarm windows on the way back down. It is the backlog, not a new fault. How the windows work: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).


# Enable the Agronomist level

Most set-up work — sensor parameters, calibrations, device configuration — needs the **“Agronomist”** level. The **“Service”** level is raised the same way. What each level allows: [Access levels](access-levels.md).

You need the PIN of this panel. It is different for every panel; take it from the device passport or ask the service support.

::: steps
1. On the home screen press **“MENU”**. The main menu opens.

   ![The main menu.](figures/menu-main)

2. Select **“Settings”** with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and press **“MENU”**. The **“Settings”** menu opens.

   ![The Settings menu at the Operator level.](figures/menu-settings)

3. Press **“DOWN”** until **“User”** is selected — it is near the end of the menu. Press **“PLUS”** until it reads **“Agronomist”** (or **“Service”**).

   ![“User” set to Agronomist.](figures/menu-user-agronomist)

4. Press **“MENU”**. The PIN pad opens. Its heading names the level you chose — **“Agronomist”** — followed by the code of this panel; have that code at hand when you ask the service support for the PIN. Type the PIN and touch **“OK”**.

   ![The PIN pad. The code beside the prompt is covered in this manual.](figures/pin-entry)

5. The **“Settings”** menu returns, now with the items of the new level — for example **“Seeding machine parameters”**. Press **“BACK”** to leave.
:::

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **At “Agronomist” and “Service” no alarm windows are shown.** When you have finished, return to **“Operator”**: repeat steps 1–3, choose **“Operator”** with **“MINUS”** and press **“MENU”** — no PIN is asked going down. Switching the panel off and on does the same.

When you come back down, the alarms that are still true are shown one after another. See [Access levels](access-levels.md#what-happens-to-the-alarms-while-the-level-is-high).


# The profile

The profile tells the panel **which devices, and how many of each**, are on the machine. A panel usually arrives with the profile already set. **Check it before you set anything else**: a device missing from the profile is never watched, and a device in the profile that is not fitted raises **“Connection lost”**.

## Check the profile on the home screen

Switch the panel on and wait a few seconds. Then look at the home screen:

- **No “Connection lost” alarm** — the panel has found every device the profile declares.
- **No white indicators with an exclamation mark** — no device is left out of control.
- **No red indicators with an “X”** — every device answers.

What the indicators mean: [Indicators](indicators.md). How to take a device into control or out of it: [Take a sensor in and out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).

> **NOTE**
>
> A profile is sometimes supplied with devices that are **not in the delivery**, so that the system can be extended later. Those indicators stay out of control on purpose. Do not switch their control on.

## Open the profile

The profile is at the **“Service”** level: raise the level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md) — choose **“Service”**), then **“MENU”** → **“Service”** → **“Profile”**.

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-profile"}
1. **“Seed sensors”** — the number of seed sensors. The selected item shows its value between **–** and **+**: change it with **“MINUS”** / **“PLUS”**.
2. **“Fertilizer sensors”** — dry fertilizer sensors.
3. **“Liquid fertilizer flow sensors”** — liquid fertilizer section sensors.
4. **“Hoppers”** — hopper level sensors.
5. **“Dispensers”** — dispenser shaft sensors.
6. **“Speed”** — where the travel speed comes from.
7. **“Fans”** — fan speed sensors.
8. **“Pressure sensors”** — air pressure sensors.
9. **Scroll bar.** More items follow below — see the table.

The top of the **“Profile”** menu of a drill with eight seed rows, two hoppers, two dispensers and one fan.
:::

## The profile items

| Item | Range |
| --- | --- |
| **“Seed sensors”** | **2 … 120.** The menu lets you enter 1, but such a profile is refused when it is saved. |
| **“Fertilizer sensors”** | **0 … 60**; seed and fertilizer sensors together **not more than 120**. |
| **“Liquid fertilizer flow sensors”** | **0 … 60** |
| **“Hoppers”** | 0 … 9 |
| **“Dispensers”** | 0 … 9 |
| **“Speed”** | **“No”** / **“Control panel”** (sensor wired to the panel) / **“Input device”** (one wheel sensor on the input device) / **“Input device (2)”** (two wheel sensors on the input device). |
| **“Fans”** | 0 … 2 |
| **“Pressure sensors”** | 0 … 3 |
| **“Work position sensor”** | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Markers”** | **“No”** / **“One”** / **“Both”** |
| **“No battery charge”**, **“Emergency oil pressure”**, **“Ignition”**, **“Low fuel”**, **“Air filter”** | The engine sensors — **“No”** / **“Yes”** each. |
| **“Seed dispenser motors”** | **0 … 60** |
| **“Fertilizer dispenser motors”** | **0 … 30**; both motor groups together **not more than 60**. |
| **“Tramline actuators”** | 0 … 4 |
| **“Liquid fertilizer pump controller”** | 0 … 1 |

On a panel built for a system without electric motors, the two motor items are not in the menu.

## When the panel refuses a profile

The panel checks the whole profile, not only the item you changed. It refuses a profile when:

- the hopper, dispenser and engine sensors together come to **more than 12**;
- they come to **more than 10** while the pressure and fan sensors together come to more than four;
- the pressure and fan sensors together come to **more than five**;
- there are **fertilizer motors but no seed motors**, or fertilizer motors but no fertilizer sensors;
- there are electric motors or a liquid fertilizer pump **but no speed sensor**;
- liquid fertilizer **valves and a pump controller** are declared at the same time.

## Save the profile

::: steps
1. After changing the profile, select **“Save profile”** at the end of the **“Profile”** menu and press **“MENU”**. The panel asks **“Are you sure?”**.

   ![The confirmation window.](figures/confirm-sure)

2. Touch **“Yes”**. The panel shows **“Wait...”**, then **“Saved”** and **“Restart system”**, and restarts by itself.
:::

If nothing was changed, the panel only shows **“No changes”**. If the profile breaks one of the rules above, it shows **“Invalid profile!”** in red and saves nothing.

Saving all the settings of a profile, and moving them on a memory card: [Save and load settings](save-and-load-settings.md).


# Save and load settings

For the current profile the panel can **save all the settings** and restore them later — useful before you try something out. With a memory card in the slot, a profile can also be saved to the card together with its settings, so one panel can serve several implements.

| Item in the **“Profile”** menu | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **“Save settings”** / **“Load settings”** | Keep a copy of the settings inside the panel, and bring it back. |
| **“Save to SD-card”** / **“Load from SD-card”** | The same with the memory card; the profile travels with its settings. Without a card, saving ends with **“Insert SD-card”**. |

At the **“Service”** level the menu also holds **“Save factory defaults”**: after **“Are you sure?”** it saves the settings as **“Save settings”** does and also keeps them, with the profile, as the panel's factory copy, which no menu item of this firmware loads back.

::: steps
1. Raise the level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md) — choose **“Service”**) and open **“MENU”** → **“Service”** → **“Profile”** ([The profile](profile.md)).

2. Scroll down to the item you need and press **“MENU”**. **“Save settings”** and **“Load settings”** ask **“Are you sure?”**.

   ![The confirmation window.](figures/confirm-sure)

3. Touch **“Yes”**. The panel answers **“Saved”** or **“Loaded”**.

   ![The panel confirms with “Saved”.](figures/info-saved)
:::

## Profile files on the memory card

- Files are named automatically **P0001.pfl** and stored in the **PROFILES** folder of the card. You may rename a file — keep the name to eight characters, Latin letters and digits.
- **“Load from SD-card”** opens a list of the profiles on the card. A profile file written by one firmware version is very likely **not readable** by another: an incompatible profile is shown in **red** in that list.


# The Settings menu

The **“Settings”** menu holds the settings of the panel itself. Open it from the home screen: **“MENU”** → **“Settings”**. The settings of the individual sensors are elsewhere — see [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-settings"}
1. **“Brightness,%”** — the backlight. **“AUTO”** lets the panel set it from its light sensor.
2. **“Volume”** — the loudness of the panel's sounds.
3. **“Language”** — the language of the screens.
4. **“Buttons sound”** — a sound on every button press.
5. **“Seeding diagram settings”** — how the seed diagram is drawn. [Below](#diagram-settings).
6. **“Change Date&Time”** — the clock. [Below](#change-date-and-time).
7. **“Alarm delay”** — how long a fault must last before the alarm window opens.
8. **“Seeding machine parameters”** — width, modes, tramline, calibrations. [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md).
9. **Scroll bar.** More items follow below.

The **“Settings”** menu of a drill with a speed sensor, at the **“Agronomist”** level.
:::

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The menu does not always have the same items.** The access level, the machine in the profile and the display mode of the diagrams change it. If an item named here is missing, check those three before looking for a fault.

## The items

| Item | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Brightness,%”** | 0 … 100, in steps of 10. **At 0 the item reads “AUTO”** and the panel sets the backlight from its light sensor — brightening quickly, dimming slowly. Any other value fixes the backlight. | Operator |
| **“Volume”** | 0 … 100, in steps of 10 | Operator |
| **“Language”** | the installed languages | Operator |
| **“Buttons sound”** | **“No”** / **“Yes”** | Operator |
| **“Seeding diagram settings”**, **“Fertilizer diagram settings”**, **“Liquid fertilizer diagram settings”** | Submenus. Each is shown only when the machine has a speed sensor, its own sensors are in the profile and its diagram is **not** in the **“Flow”** mode. | Operator |
| **“Change Date&Time”** | submenu | Operator |
| **“Alarm delay”** | **2 … 20 s**, default 3 s. See [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md). | Operator |
| **“Product rate error,%”** | **3 … 20 %**. Shown only when a product is dosed by weight or a liquid fertilizer pump controller is in the profile. | Agronomist |
| **“Seeding machine parameters”** | Submenu. Hidden when the machine has neither a speed sensor nor a tramline actuator. | Agronomist |
| **“User”** | The access level — see [Access levels](access-levels.md). | Operator |
| **“Reset settings”** | Returns this menu to the factory values. | Service |

On a machine with two groups of seed sensors, the two diagram items read **“Seeding gr.A diagram”** and **“Seeding gr.B diagram”**.

**The settings are saved by themselves** a few seconds after the last press. Wait a moment before you switch the panel off.

## Diagram settings

![The diagram settings of the seed sensors.](figures/nast-seedgraph)

There are three of these menus — seed, dry fertilizer, liquid fertilizer — with the same items:

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **“Skips & Doubles”** | Shows the skip and double bars over the last stretch of the path. **“Precise” mode only.** |
| **“Grid”** | **“No”** — only the rate line; **“Partial”** — only the tolerance limits; **“Full”** — both. |
| **“Scale S&D,%”** | The height of the skip and double bars, **5 … 50 %** in steps of 5. **“Precise” mode only.** |
| **“Reset to defaults”** | Returns this menu to the factory values. **Service** level only. |

## Change Date and Time

::: steps
1. Select **“Change Date&Time”** and press **“MENU”**. The date and time fields open.

   ![The date and time fields.](figures/menu-datetime)

2. Select each field with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and set it with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**.

3. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”**. The clock takes the new values. **“BACK”** instead leaves the clock unchanged.
:::


# Seeding machine parameters

**“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”**. The item needs the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)) and is hidden on a machine with neither a speed sensor nor a tramline actuator. Which items it holds depends on the profile.

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-seeding"}
1. **“Width, cm”** — the working width. The selected value stands between **–[** and **]+**.
2. **“Mode of seeding”** — **“Flow”**, **“Hybrid”** or **“Precise”**.
3. **“Tramline”** — the tramline submenu.
4. **“Speed calibration”** — starts the speed calibration.
5. **“Reset to defaults”** — factory values for this menu. **Service** level only.

The menu of a precision planter with a speed sensor and no fertilizer, dispensers or liquid fertilizer.
:::

## Width, cm

The working width of the implement. The worked area is calculated from it, so it must be entered. Press **“MENU”** on the item: the number pad opens. Type the digits — the key at the top right deletes the last one — and touch **“OK”** to accept, or press **“BACK”** to keep the old value.

![The number pad for “Width, cm”.](figures/menu-keypad)

## Mode of seeding, Mode of fertilizers

Three modes each:

| Mode | Unit | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Flow”** | seeds per second | grain drills |
| **“Hybrid”** | seeds per metre | grain drills — recommended |
| **“Precise”** | seeds per metre, with skips and doubles counted | precision planters |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Switching between “Precise” and the other two modes demands a reset of the statistics** if any field has work recorded in it.

## Mode of liquid fertilizer

**“Flow”** (litres per minute) or **“By area”** (litres per hectare). **Shown only when there is no liquid fertilizer pump controller in the profile** — with a controller the panel chooses the mode itself.

## Actuators to sensors mapping

Which section sensors belong to which tramline actuator or electric motor. When that actuator shuts its sections off, their sensors switch to tramline monitoring.

![The mapping screen: one line for the actuators, one for the motors.](figures/menu-mapping)

A mapping is a **range**: **“Range start”** and **“Range end”** — equal numbers mean a single section. Up to **four ranges** can be attached to one actuator. On a machine with metering motors the screen also has **“Motors to sensors mapping”**.

## Tramline

The rhythms of the tramline, in a submenu of its own with two items: **“Tramline”** (**“No”** / **“Yes”**) and **“Tramline rhythm settings”**.

![The tramline submenu.](figures/menu-tramline)

Setting up a rhythm: [Tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).

## Speed calibration and Dispenser calibration

The two calibrations that need the machine to move. **“Dispenser calibration”** carries a number beside it: the dispenser to calibrate, or **0** for all of them at once.

- [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md)
- [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md)


# Sensor settings

Every sensor, actuator and motor on the machine has its own settings and its own status screen. Both are reached from the home screen. The parameters of each kind of sensor are in the topics that follow this one.

## Reach a sensor

::: steps
1. On the home screen **hold “MENU”** for a few seconds. The panel enters the sensor setting mode; the selected sensor is drawn inside a white rectangle.

2. Move from sensor to sensor with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”**. **“PLUS”** takes the selected sensor into control, **“MINUS”** takes it out — see [Take a sensor in and out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).

3. Press **“MENU”**. The context menu of the selected sensor opens.

   ![The context menu of the speed sensor.](figures/ctx-speed)

4. Press **“BACK”** to leave the mode.
:::

Holding a sensor tile on the screen opens the same context menu directly.

## The context menu

::: {.anatomy fig="ctx-fan"}
1. **“Information”** — opens the status screen of this sensor. [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).
2. **“Disable control”** / **“Enable control”** — takes the sensor out of monitoring, or back in. The first time in a session the panel asks for confirmation.
3. **The parameters of this sensor** — here the three of a fan sensor. Which of them you see depends on the access level.
4. **The current value.** Select the line; the value stands between **–** and **+** and changes with **“MINUS”** / **“PLUS”**.
5. **“Reset to defaults”** — returns this sensor's parameters to the factory values. **Service** level only.

The context menu of a fan sensor at the **“Agronomist”** level.
:::

![The confirmation asked before control is switched off.](figures/confirm-disable-control)

## The status screen

**“Information”** opens the status screen of the sensor: its identity, its link, its live figures and its active alarms. How to read it: [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

## Calibrations

Four calibrations exist. They are not variants of one procedure: each writes different parameters and is reached a different way.

| What it puts right | Where | Level | Machine |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Travel speed — the pulses of the speed sensor over a known distance. [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md) | **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Speed calibration”** | Agronomist | drives 100 m |
| Dispenser rotation — **“Wheel, pulses”** against **“Dispenser pulses”**. [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md) | **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Dispenser calibration”** | Agronomist | wheel and dispenser shaft turned together |
| Dispenser mass — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Weight, pulses”**. [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md) | context menu of the dispenser sensor | Operator | standing |
| Metering roller mass — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”** of one motor. [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md) | context menu of the dispenser electric motor | Operator | standing |

The two menu calibrations need the **“Agronomist”** level, like the menu that leads to them. The two mass calibrations are at the **“Operator”** level, because they have to be repeated whenever the product changes.


# The sensor status screen

Reached through **“Information”** in the context menu of a sensor ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)). It shows what the panel knows about one sensor.

## The screen

::: {.anatomy fig="status-hopper"}
1. **“Channel #”** — which sensor of the whole list this is.
2. **Previous sensor** — or press **“MINUS”**. The screen stays open.
3. **Next sensor** — or press **“PLUS”**.
4. **“Address:”** — the address the sensor answers on. Not shown in this manual.
5. **“Type:”** — the kind of sensor and its number, here hopper sensor 1. Some sensors show a line **“Unit:”** instead of the address — where they are connected, for example **“Control panel”**.
6. **“Link:”** — the state of the communication. [Table below](#link-states).
7. **The figures of this kind of sensor** — here the level on the input of a hopper sensor. [Table below](#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).
8. **“Alarm 1 from 1”** — the active alarms, one at a time. **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** step through them.
9. **The name of the alarm** shown.

The status screen of a hopper sensor whose hopper is empty.
:::

| Button | Action |
| --- | --- |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Next / previous sensor — the screen stays open. |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Step through the active alarms of this sensor. |
| **“MENU”** | The context menu of this sensor. |
| **“BACK”** | Back to the sensor selection. |

## Link states

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **“Normal”** | The sensor answers. |
| **“Not controlled”** | The sensor is out of control: neither the communication nor anything else is watched. |
| **“No connection”** | The sensor does not answer. Red. |
| **“Wrong device type!”** | Something answers, but not the kind of device the profile expects. Red. |
| **“IMITATION”** | Speed sensor only: the speed is simulated, not measured. Yellow. |

The figures are drawn only while the sensor is **under control**, answers, and is of the expected kind. A sensor out of control shows its identity and nothing else.

## What each kind of sensor adds

![The status screen of a speed sensor wired to the panel.](figures/status-speed)

| Sensor | What the screen shows |
| --- | --- |
| Speed sensor | The pulse frequency **F=** in Hz; with two speed sensors **F1=** and **F2=**. Under it the two limits **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”**. On a machine that doses a product by weight with electric motors, the limits are those the motors can hold, narrowed by the two settings; a limit the settings cannot meet is written in red as an inequality. Without such motors a limit set to zero is shown as **----**, switched off. |
| Hopper sensor | **Pin:** and the level on the input, **"0"** or **"1"**. |
| Dispenser shaft sensor | **F=** in Hz, to three decimals. |
| Fan sensor | **F=** in Hz. |
| Pressure sensor | **P=** in kPa. |
| Seed sensor, dry fertilizer sensor | **Status:** and one of eight states — [below](#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor). |
| Liquid fertilizer flow sensor | **Status:** **Working**, or **Working:Tramline** in the tramline mode; under it **Flow=** in L/min. |
| Work position sensor | **Position: Working** or **Position: Transporting**, and **Pin:** with the level on the input. |
| Ignition, oil pressure, battery charge, fuel level, air filter | **Pin:** and the level on the input, **"0"** or **"1"**. |
| Marker sensor | Only the common lines. |
| Tramline actuator | **Status:** **Pulled in**, **Pulled out**, **Working** while the shutter moves, or **Unknown**. |
| Dispenser electric motor | **Status:** **Working**, or **Faulty** while any alarm of the motor is active; then **Last fault:** with the controller's code, if there has been one ([codes](motor-fault-codes.md)). A universal controller adds **IN1[ ] IN2[ ] IN3[ ]** with the levels on its three inputs. |
| Liquid fertilizer pump controller | **Status:** **Working** or **Faulty**. With a fault, **Last fault:** and the code. Without one: **Flow=** in L/min, **Load=** in per cent, and **Pressure sensor: No** if there is none, otherwise **Pressure sensor=** in Bar with the raw signal in mA in brackets. Dashes stand for a value the controller cannot give. |

## The eight states of a seed or fertilizer sensor

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Working** | Normal. |
| **Working:Tramline** | Normal; the sensor is in the tramline control mode for the current bout. |
| **Configuring** | The sensor has received new settings and is applying them. |
| **Calibration in progress** | The sensor runs its initial calibration. It takes a few seconds. |
| **Clogged** | The infrared emitter of the optical channel is blocked — most likely a blocked seed tube. Red. |
| **Light struck** | Too much sunlight falls into the optical channel; the sensor may miscount. Red. |
| **Faulty** | The sensor has failed and must be replaced. Red. |
| **Unknown** | Another fault that cannot be identified. Red. |



# Travel speed sensor

Everything the panel counts — area, rates, deviations — is worked out from the distance travelled. **A speed sensor that is out by a tenth makes every other figure on the panel wrong by a tenth.** Set its parameters first, then calibrate it ([Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md)).

Open the context menu of the speed sensor as described in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md). All its parameters need the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)).

![The context menu of the speed sensor. A limit that is switched off reads “No”.](figures/ctx-speed)

The context menu also offers **“Speed calibration”** directly, under **“Information”**.

| Parameter | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Pulses”** | The pulse figure of the sensor. Set it before the calibration, which corrects it. | 1 … 1000 |
| **“Count period”** | How many pulses of the sensor the panel averages the travel speed over; a higher value gives a steadier figure. Acts only on a speed sensor wired to the panel itself. | 1 … 1000 |
| **“Diameter, cm”** | The wheel diameter. Set it before the calibration. | 10 … 200 |
| **“Factor, %”** | The drive ratio to the wheel; 100 is a direct 1 : 1 drive. | 1 … 10000 |
| **“Seeding criteria”** | **“Yes”**: the alarms of the seed, dry fertilizer and liquid fertilizer sections are raised only while the machine moves. **“No”**: also while it stands. Hidden, and always **“Yes”**, in the **“Precise”** mode and on machines with metering motors or a liquid fertilizer pump controller. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Min speed, km/h”** | Below this speed the home screen shows **“FASTER”**. **0 switches the check off.** | 0 … 99 |
| **“Max speed, km/h”** | Above this speed the home screen shows **“SLOWER”**. **0 switches the check off.** | 0 … 99 |
| **“Imitation, km/h”** | A simulated speed. **0** = the real sensor is used. | **0 … 20** |
| **“Width, cm”** | The track between the two wheels of a two-sensor installation. | 0 … 10000 |
| **“GPS”**, **“GPS internal”** | Take the speed from a receiver instead of the wheel. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |

The minimum must be below the maximum, otherwise the panel raises **“Error in settings of Min/Max”** ([Speed sensor alarms](alarms-speed-sensor.md)).

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Setting “Imitation, km/h” to anything but zero changes two other things by itself.** The panel sets **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** to zero — they mean nothing against a simulated speed — and it **locks the product application**, so that nothing is dosed while the machine stands. The lock is the hand icon on the home screen; hold **“HOME”** to release it ([Lock the application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md)).

The imitated speed is also **held inside the range the dosing allows**: a value outside it is pulled back to the nearest limit as you enter it. While the speed is imitated, the status screen of the sensor shows **“IMITATION”** in yellow. Working without a speed sensor: [Work without a speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md).

## The status screen

The status screen shows the pulse frequency **F=** in Hz (with two sensors **F1=** and **F2=**) and the two limits in force. See [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).

![The status screen of a speed sensor wired to the panel.](figures/status-speed)


# Calibrate the speed sensor

The calibration corrects the pulse figure of the speed sensor against a known distance. **Before you start, set “Pulses” and “Diameter, cm”** of the sensor ([Travel speed sensor](speed-sensor.md)) — the calibration corrects the pulse figure; it cannot invent it. You need the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)).

::: steps
1. Mark out **100 m** on level ground and put the machine at the start.

2. Open **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”**, select **“Speed calibration”** and press **“MENU”**. The panel shows **“Pass 100m and press STOP”** with a single **“STOP”** button.

   ![The speed calibration window.](figures/calib-speed)

3. Drive the marked distance and stop at the end.

4. Touch **“STOP”**. The panel shows **“Done”** and closes the window by itself.

   ![The panel confirms with “Done”.](figures/info-done)
:::

The distance is fixed at 100 m; the panel does not ask for it. It waits half a second after **“STOP”** before reading the counter and checks the connection once more in that moment — a sensor that drops out on the last metre is reported as a lost connection, not as a bad result.

## When it does not work

| The panel shows | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **“No speed sensor”** | The profile has no speed sensor. The calibration does not start. |
| **“Connection lost with the sensor! Calibration canceled!”** | The sensor does not answer. |
| **“Sensor not controlled! Calibration canceled!”** | The sensor is out of control. Take it into control ([Take a sensor in and out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md)). |
| **“FAILURE! The tractor did not move!”** | The counter did not move: the sensor gave no pulses at all — not an inaccurate reading, none. Check the sensor and its cable. |
| **“Calibration canceled!”** | The window was closed some other way than with **“STOP”**. Nothing has changed. |


# Seed sensors and dry fertilizer sensors

Seed sensors and dry fertilizer sensors are the same kind of device and share one parameter set. **Almost everything here is common to the whole group**: change it on one sensor and it changes for all sensors of the group. Only two things are set per sensor — whether it is **under control** (**“Disable control”** / **“Enable control”**) and **“Product application”**. Open the context menu of any sensor of the group as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of a seed sensor, top part.](figures/ctx-seed)

| Parameter | What it does | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Flow rate”** | The rate for the **“Flow”** mode, in seeds per second. Below it the section raises the low-rate alarm. | 1 … 1500 | Operator |
| **“Hybrid rate”** | The target in the **“Hybrid”** mode. | 1 … 200 | Operator |
| **“Precise rate,x10”** | The target in the **“Precise”** mode, in tenths. | 5 … 500 | Operator |
| **“Sensitivity”** | The sensitivity of sensors of an older generation; the panel sends it to them. Shown only when such a sensor is connected. | 1 … 120 | Agronomist |
| **“Fraction”** | The count filter of the sensors, set for the size of the seed or granule; the panel sends it to every sensor of the group. The rate, skip and double alarms tell you which way to change it. | 1 … 100 | Operator |
| **“Correction”** | A fine adjustment of seed detection for the sensor generation that uses it; the panel sends it to those sensors only, and the item appears only when one is connected. Default 300. | 100 … 3300, steps of 10 | Operator |
| **“Rate error,%”** | How far the actual rate may stand from the target before an alarm. | 5 … 95, steps of 5 | Agronomist |
| **“Doubles error,%”** | The share of doubles that raises an alarm. **“Precise” mode only.** | 0 … 95 | Agronomist |
| **“Skips error,%”** | The share of skips that raises an alarm. **“Precise” mode only.** | 0 … 95 | Agronomist |
| **“Recalculation,m”** / **“Recalculation,sec”** | The stretch the skips and doubles are counted over — in metres or in seconds, depending on the mode. | 10 … 50 | Operator |
| **“Percent of sowing,%”** | The share of the seed rows under control that must sow before the panel takes the drill as seeding; until then the seed and dry fertilizer sensors raise no rate, skip, double or tramline alarm. Seed sensors only; hidden on machines with metering motors or a liquid fertilizer pump controller. | 5 … 80, steps of 5 | Agronomist |
| **“Tolerable sowing to tramline,%”** | How much a section that should be shut off for the tramline may still deliver. | 0 … 50 | Agronomist |
| **“Group start address”** | Set at commissioning — see [Device configuration](device-configuration.md). | | Service |

> **TIP**
>
> **“Fraction” is the first setting to look at when the rate alarms do not match reality.** Most rate, skip and double alarms name it, with the direction to change it: [Rate alarms](alarms-rate.md), [Doubles and skips](alarms-seeding-quality.md), [Tramline alarms](alarms-tramline.md).

The target rates themselves are changed while you work, on the home screen — see [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md). The status screen of these sensors shows one of eight states — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor). If a sensor reports **“Clogged”**, **“Light struck”** or **“Broken”**: [Sensor clogged or broken](alarms-sensor-state.md).


# Liquid fertilizer sensors and pump controller

Liquid fertilizer is watched by flow sensors in the sections; on some machines a pump controller also drives the pump to the rate. Open the context menu of either as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

## Liquid fertilizer section sensors

| Parameter | What it does | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Pulses per liter”** | The pulses the flow sensor gives per litre; the panel turns them into litres per minute, litres per hectare and the volume applied. Hidden when a pump controller is in the profile — the controller's figures are used then. | 1 … 60000 | Agronomist |
| **“Rate error,%”** | How far the actual rate may stand from the target before an alarm. | 5 … 95, steps of 5 | Agronomist |
| **“Tolerable leak to tramline,%”** | How much a section shut off for the tramline may still deliver. | 0 … 50 | Agronomist |
| **“Group start address”** | See [Device configuration](device-configuration.md). | | Service |

The two target rates of this sensor — one for the **“Flow”** mode, one for the **“By area”** mode — have **no menu item**. They are set on the home screen with **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”**, like every other target rate ([Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md)). The mode itself: [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md#mode-of-liquid-fertilizer).

## Liquid fertilizer pump controller

| Parameter | What it does | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Pulses per liter”** | How many pulses of the pump drive make one litre; the panel works out the volume applied from it. The figure is kept in the pump controller: the panel reads it at start-up and writes a change back to it. | 100 … 10000, steps of 10 | Agronomist |
| **“Pressure sensor”** | Which pressure sensor watches the supply line. | 0 … 2 | Agronomist |
| **“Pressure boundary, Bar”** | The pressure the pressure sensor reads at the top of its range, from the sensor's specification; the panel scales the line pressure with it. Default 16.0 bar. | 0.0 … 50.0 | Agronomist |
| **“Max pressure, Bar”** | Above it the controller raises **“High pressure”**. | 0.0 … 50.0 | Operator |
| **“Section control D.I.”** | Has no effect in this firmware: the panel does not read this input for the pump. | **“No”** / **“Shut off(0)”** / **“Shut off(1)”** | Agronomist |
| **“Start delay,mS”** | The shortest time between two starts of the pump: a start that would come sooner waits until this time has passed. Default 30 ms. | 0 … 500, steps of 5 | Service |
| **“Group start address”** | See [Device configuration](device-configuration.md). | | Agronomist |

The status screen of the pump controller shows the flow, the pump load and the line pressure — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds). Alarms: [Liquid fertilizer pump](alarms-pump-controller.md), [Rate alarms](alarms-rate.md).


# Dispenser shaft sensor

The dispenser shaft sensor counts the turns of a dispenser driven from the ground wheel. The panel can watch it two ways: by its **rotation** against the speed sensor, or by the **mass** of product it applies. Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of a dispenser sensor with both controls switched off.](figures/ctx-dispenser)

| Parameter | What it does | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Period, s”** | The longest time between two shaft pulses. If the shaft gives no pulse for longer while the machine sows or moves, the panel raises **“No rotation”**. Default 10 s. | 1 … 60 | Operator |
| **“Rotation speed control”** | Watch the shaft rotation against the travel speed. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** | Agronomist |
| **“Wheel, pulses”** | Set by the rotation calibration. | 1 … 65535 | Agronomist |
| **“Dispenser pulses”** | Set by the rotation calibration. | 1 … 65535 | Agronomist |
| **“Maximum error, %”** | How far the shaft speed may stand from the speed the travel speed calls for; beyond it, while the machine moves, the panel raises **“Low speed of rotation”** or **“High speed of rotation”**. Shown only when **“Rotation speed control”** is **“Yes”**. Default 10 %. | 1 … 50 | Agronomist |
| **“Weight control”** | Watch the dispenser by the **mass** applied instead of by its rotation. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** | Agronomist |
| **“Type of product”** | Which product this dispenser meters. | | Agronomist |
| **“Weight, gr”** / **“Weight, pulses”** | Both set by the calibration by weight. | 1 … 65535 each | Agronomist |

With **“Weight control”** switched on, the context menu also holds **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”**.

> **TIP**
>
> **Prefer weight control to rotation control.** Rotation control notices that the shaft has stopped, not that the product has. **“Weight control”** watches the kilograms per hectare applied and catches an empty or bridged hopper whose dispenser still turns.

## Calibrations

- **Rotation** — for **“Rotation speed control”**: [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md).
- **Mass** — for **“Weight control”**; repeat it whenever the product changes: [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md).

The status screen shows the shaft pulse frequency **F=** in Hz, to three decimals. Its alarms: [Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms](alarms-rotation.md), and with weight control [Dosing by weight](alarms-dosing-by-weight.md).


# Calibrate the dispenser rotation

This calibration teaches the panel how many dispenser shaft pulses belong to one wheel pulse, so that it can tell a stopped shaft from a moving machine. It is the basis of **“Rotation speed control”** of the dispenser sensor ([Dispenser sensor](dispenser-sensor.md)). It writes **“Wheel, pulses”** and **“Dispenser pulses”**.

**Before you start:** the speed sensor **and** every dispenser taking part must be under control and answering. You need the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)).

::: steps
1. Open **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Dispenser calibration”**. Set the number of the dispenser with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** — or **0** for all of them at once — and press **“MENU”**. The panel shows **“Calibration”** and a progress bar.

   ![The progress bar of the dispenser calibration.](figures/calib-dispenser-progress)

2. Turn the drive wheel and the dispenser shaft together — by hand, or by moving the machine. The bar fills as the counters rise.

3. Keep turning until the bar reaches 100 %. That happens when the speed sensor **and every** dispenser taking part have each given at least **100 pulses**. The bar follows whichever is furthest behind — a dispenser that does not turn holds it at zero.

4. At 100 % the panel beeps once and shows **“Stop rotation!”**. Stop everything.

5. The panel waits until no counter has changed for **two seconds**, then writes the result and shows **“Done”**.
:::

**“To abort operation press BACK.”** stands at the bottom of the screen; **“BACK”** stops the calibration at any moment.

If any sensor taking part is out of control or does not answer, the calibration ends with **“Sensor not controlled! Calibration canceled!”** or **“Connection lost with the sensor! Calibration canceled!”**.

> **NOTE**
>
> **The stored numbers are not the ones you watched.** If the counts do not fit the parameter range, the panel halves **both** numbers together, again and again, until they fit. The ratio is kept; only the two stored figures come out smaller than what was counted.


# Calibrate the dispenser by weight

This calibration stores how many grams one dispenser shaft pulse delivers — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Weight, pulses”** of the dispenser sensor. Repeat it whenever the product changes. It is done standing, at the **“Operator”** level; the panel raises itself to **“Agronomist”** for the length of the calibration and puts the level back on exit.

**You need:** a container that holds 2 to 60 kg of the product, and scales.

The item is only there when **“Weight control”** is switched on for this dispenser ([Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md)).

::: steps
1. Hold the tile of the dispenser sensor and choose **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”**. The first screen lists the target rates of the products in use, in kg/ha; the product of this dispenser is marked with **>** and **<**.

2. Touch **“Calibrate dispenser N”** (or press **“PLUS”**). If the dispenser cannot be calibrated, a red line stands there instead with the reason: **“Not controlled”**, **“No connection”** or **“FAILURE”**. **“Exit”** (or **“BACK”**) leaves.

3. The second screen gives the preparation. Weigh the empty container and write the weight down.

4. Fill the hopper with the product and place the empty container under the dispenser.

5. Turn the rotor until its cells are filled. **This matters more than it looks:** a rotor with empty cells gives short measure for the first turns, and that error lands in the stored figure.

6. Touch **“Go to calibration”** (or press **“UP”**). **“Cancel”** (or **“BACK”**) steps back. The third screen counts **“Impulses”** and turns a rotor icon as they arrive.

7. Empty the container and place it under the dispenser again.

8. Turn the dispenser rotor and fill the container as far as possible — **not less than 2 kg and not more than 60 kg**.

9. Touch **“Complete”** (or press **“MINUS”**). The button appears only after **more than ten pulses**. **“Cancel”** asks **“Are you sure?”** before throwing the measurement away.

10. Weigh the filled container. The number pad asks to **“Enter the difference of the filled and empty container in grams”**. Type the weight of the product alone — **2000 to 60000 g**; the pad offers 10000 — and touch **“OK”**. The panel stores **“Weight, gr”** and **“Weight, pulses”**.
:::

> **NOTE**
>
> **A dispenser alarm during the calibration does not stop it** — only a lost connection does. The measurement is mechanical, and the panel keeps out of the way until the container is weighed.


# Dispenser electric motor

An electric motor drives a dispenser at the speed the panel works out from the target rate and the travel speed. Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of a metering motor, top part.](figures/ctx-motor)

| Parameter | What it does | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Holes in disk”** | **“Precise” mode only.** | 1 … 200 | Operator |
| **“Numerator”** / **“Denominator”** | Together: the gear ratio between the motor and the dispenser shaft. | 1 … 500 each | Agronomist |
| **“Rotation direction”** | The direction the motor turns. Set it so that the dispenser turns the right way for how the motor is fitted; default **“Forward”**. | **“Forward”** / **“Backward”** | Agronomist |
| **“Rollback when jammed”** | Back the rotor off and try again instead of stalling. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** | Agronomist |
| **“Section control D.I.”** | Lets a switch on the section-control input of the motor controller stop this motor: **“Shut off(0)”** stops it while the input reads 0, **“Shut off(1)”** while it reads 1; **“No”** ignores the input. | **“No”** / **“Shut off(0)”** / **“Shut off(1)”** | Service |
| **“Start delay,mS”** | The shortest time between the start of one metering motor and the next: a motor that would start sooner waits, so the motors start one after another. Default 30 ms. | 0 … 500, steps of 5 | Service |
| **“Group start address”** | Set at commissioning — see [Device configuration](device-configuration.md). | | Service |
| **“Type of product”** | Which of the four products this motor meters. | | Agronomist |
| **“Weight, gr”** / **“Rotations”** | Both set by the calibration by weight. | 1 … 65535 each | Agronomist |
| **“Minimum, rpm”** / **“Maximum, rpm”** | The shaft speed window the panel may use. | 0.1 … 500.0 each | Agronomist |
| **“Button input”** | Digital input of the motor controller used as a calibration button; **“No”** = none. | No, 1 … 3 | Agronomist |
| **“Activation signal”** | Which state of that input counts as pressed. | 0 / 1 | Agronomist |

![The lower part of the same menu, with the calibration item.](figures/ctx-motor-lower)

**“Minimum, rpm”** and **“Maximum, rpm”** are not a safety limit but the window the rate control works in. The dosing speed window on the calibration screen is worked out from them together with the roller figures. **“Button input”** and **“Activation signal”** let one person start the motor from the dispenser during the calibration — see [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).

The status screen shows **“Working”** or **“Faulty”** and the last fault code ([Read the fault code of an electric motor](motor-fault-codes.md)). Alarms: [Metering motor alarms](alarms-motor-controller.md), [Dosing by weight](alarms-dosing-by-weight.md). The controller itself is set up in [Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md). **“Electric motors”** in the context menu (**“Service”** level) opens the Motors screen on this motor — the same screen as **“Service”** → **“Electric motors”** ([Motor controller diagnostics](motor-controller-diagnostics.md)).


# Calibrate a metering motor by weight

This calibration stores how much product one turn of the metering roller delivers — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”** of one motor. Repeat it whenever the product or the roller changes. It is done at the **“Operator”** level.

**You need:** the machine standing still, a container that holds 1 to 60 kg of the product, and scales.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The item appears only while the machine is standing still.** In motion the panel removes it from the context menu without a message. And while the calibration is open, **every** electric motor on the machine — seed and fertilizer — is in manual mode at zero speed: nothing meters. Leaving the calibration returns them all to automatic rate control.

::: steps
1. Hold the tile of the motor and choose **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”**.

   ![The motor's context menu with the calibration item at the top.](figures/ctx-motor-lower)

2. The first screen shows the target rates and, under **“Product dosage speed limitation:”**, the **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** the current settings allow. If it reads **“Can not provide dosage!”** in red, the roller fitted cannot deliver the rate at any speed — calibration will not repair that; fit another roller. Otherwise touch **“Calibrate electric motor N”** (or press **“PLUS”**).

3. The second screen prepares the rotor. Weigh the empty container and write the weight down. Fill the hopper and place the empty container under the dispenser.

4. Touch **“Fill the rotor cells”** (or press **“MENU”**). The motor turns the driven shaft exactly **two turns** and stops by itself. **“Stop motor”** (**“BACK”**) interrupts it. Repeat until the cells are full.

5. Touch **“Go to calibration”** (or press **“UP”**). The third screen shows **“Rotations”** to one decimal.

6. Empty the container and place it under the dispenser again.

7. Touch **“Calibration”** (or press **“MENU”**): the motor runs. Touch **“Stop motor”** (or press **“BACK”**) to stop it. Run and stop as often as needed — the counter keeps a running total. Fill the container as far as possible, **not less than 1 kg and not more than 60 kg**.

8. Touch **“Complete”** (or press **“MINUS”**). It appears once more than **one full turn** has been made.

9. Weigh the filled container. The number pad asks for the difference of the filled and empty container in grams — **1000 to 60000 g**. Type it and touch **“OK”**. The panel stores **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”** for this motor.
:::

During the rotor filling the motor runs at the middle of its **“Minimum, rpm”** … **“Maximum, rpm”** window, but not faster than 60 rpm.

## Run the motor from a button at the dispenser

If **“Button input”** of the motor is set to an input (1 … 3) and **“Activation signal”** is set to match that button ([Dispenser electric motor](dispenser-motor.md)), a button on that input starts and stops the motor exactly as **“Calibration”** and **“Stop motor”** do: **the motor runs while the button is held and stops when it is released.** One person can stand at the dispenser with the container instead of walking to the cab between runs. The screen shows the same buttons whether or not such a button is set up — the panel gives no hint of it.

## When the calibration stops by itself

The calibration ends with a failure if the motor stops answering, if the motor raises an alarm, or if **ten seconds pass without pulses from the rotation sensor** — then the panel shows **“No data from rotation sensor”**. A jammed or unplugged rotation sensor ends the run rather than quietly storing zero.


# Fan sensor

The fan sensor watches the speed of the fan of a pneumatic drill or planter. Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md) — the picture there shows exactly this menu.

| Parameter | What it does | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Minimum, rpm”** | Below it the panel raises **“Low speed of rotation”**. | 500 … 9000, steps of 500 | Operator |
| **“Maximum, rpm”** | Above it the panel raises **“High speed of rotation”**. | 500 … 9000, steps of 500 | Operator |
| **“Pulses”** | How many pulses one turn of the fan gives. | 1 … 60 | Agronomist |

The status screen shows the pulse frequency **F=** in Hz. Alarms: [Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms](alarms-rotation.md).


# Pressure sensor

The pressure sensor measures the positive pressure or the vacuum of the air system. Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

| Parameter | What it does | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Filter”** | How strongly the reading is smoothed. | 1 … 16 | Agronomist |
| **“Minimum, Pa”** | The lower limit of the allowed band. | 0 … 10000, steps of 100 | Operator |
| **“Maximum, Pa”** | The upper limit of the allowed band. | 0 … 10000, steps of 100 | Operator |

The status screen shows the pressure **P=** in kPa. Alarms: [Air pressure](alarms-pressure.md). Giving a new pressure sensor its address: [Configure a pressure sensor](configure-pressure-sensor.md).


# Marker sensors

The marker sensors tell the panel which marker is down. The profile declares **“No”**, **“One”** or **“Both”** ([The profile](profile.md)). Open the context menu of a marker sensor as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

| Parameter | What it does | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Connected marker”** | **“Left”** or **“Right”**. | Agronomist |
| **“Signal "down"”** | Which state of the input means the marker is lowered. | Agronomist |

The status screen of a marker sensor shows only the common lines.

> **NOTE**
>
> **The marker sensors are wired to the tramline actuator controller.** One such controller carries the actuator **and** both marker sensors — see [Configure a tramline actuator controller](configure-tramline-actuator.md).


# Hopper, work position and engine sensors

These sensors report one of two states and nothing more. Open the context menu of any of them as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md). Their status screen shows **Pin:** and the level on the input, **"0"** or **"1"**.

## Hopper sensor

The hopper sensor has **no parameters of its own** — its context menu holds only the three common items.

![The context menu of a hopper sensor.](figures/ctx-hopper)

Alarm: [Hopper empty](alarms-hopper.md).

## Work position sensor

The work position sensor tells the panel whether the implement is lowered for work or raised for transport. The status screen shows **Position: Working** or **Position: Transporting**.

![The context menu of the work position sensor.](figures/ctx-work-position)

| Parameter | What it does | Range | Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Transporting position signal”** | Which state of the input means the transport position. | 0 / 1 | Agronomist |

The menu can also hold **“Alarms criteria”** (**“Yes”** / **“No”**, **“Agronomist”** level): with **“Yes”**, the default, the seed, fertilizer and dispenser shaft alarms are not raised while the implement is in the transport position; the item is hidden, and always **“Yes”**, on machines with metering motors or a liquid fertilizer pump controller.

## Engine sensors

**“No battery charge”**, **“Emergency oil pressure”**, **“Ignition”**, **“Low fuel”** and **“Air filter”** are five separate inputs, each switched on in the profile on its own ([The profile](profile.md)).

![The context menu of the oil pressure sensor.](figures/ctx-oil-pressure)

| Parameter | What it does | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Activation signal”** | Which state of the input is the one worth reporting. | Agronomist |
| **“Signal delay, sec”** | How long that state must hold before it counts. Defaults: **15 s** for the fuel level, **5 s** for the air filter. | Agronomist |

Alarms: [Tractor engine alarms](alarms-tractor.md).


# Tramline actuator

The tramline actuator shuts the sections of the tramline bout. It has two parameters of its own, in its context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)):

| Parameter | Values | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Cutoff position”** | **“Pulled out”** / **“Pulled in”** — the position of the actuator in which its sections are shut off. Default **“Pulled out”**. | Agronomist |
| **“Switch”** | **“when seeding”** / **“always”** — when the actuator is switched. Default **“when seeding”**. | Agronomist |

The rest of its settings live elsewhere:

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| The address and the marker channels of its controller | [Configure a tramline actuator controller](configure-tramline-actuator.md) |
| The rhythm — which bout shuts which actuator | [Tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md) |
| Which sections belong to the actuator | **“Actuators to sensors mapping”** — [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md#actuators-to-sensors-mapping) |

The status screen of the actuator shows **Status:** **Pulled in**, **Pulled out**, **Working** while the shutter is moving, or **Unknown**. Alarms: [Tramline alarms](alarms-tramline.md).

> **NOTE**
>
> **One actuator controller carries three things:** the actuator itself and **both** marker sensors of the bout. That is why a machine with markers and a tramline needs only one such controller.


# Device configuration — before you start

When a system is commissioned, or a sensor is replaced, each new device must be given its address — the number by which the panel finds it on the sensor network. That is done in **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”**, one device at a time.

> **WARNING**
>
> **For authorised service engineers.** A device given the wrong address disappears from the panel or takes the place of another one. Follow these topics or the instructions of an Agriwelt GmbH engineer, and do not try menu items at random.

## Prepare

::: steps
1. **Disconnect every sensor** from the network connector of the panel.

2. **Connect only the one device** that is to be given a new address.

3. Switch the panel on. Alarms about lost communication appear — close them all ([How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md)).

4. Raise the access level to **“Agronomist”** — see [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

5. Press **“BACK”**, then choose **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”**. The menu offers four kinds of device.

   ![The “Sensors Configuration” menu.](figures/menu-sensorcfg)
:::

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **One device on the cable at a time.** The panel addresses whatever answers. With two devices of the same kind connected, which of them takes the new address is not defined.

## The pattern

All four menus work the same way:

| Item | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **“Sensor address”** / **“Device address”** | Which device the menu talks to. Leave it at **“AUTO”** and the panel talks to the single device that answers. Pressing **“MENU”** on this item starts a **search**; each further press steps to the next device found. |
| **“New address”** | The address the device is to take. Set it with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**. |
| **“Set”** | Writes it. **“Done”** means the device has accepted it. |

> **CAUTION**
>
> **“MENU” on the address item is not a harmless look.** It starts a search on the network and can change what the connected devices answer to. Use it only with a single device on the cable, never on an assembled machine.

**Afterwards, every time:** disconnect the device and connect it again, return to the home screen and check that it appears where it should. Then set the level back to **“Operator”** — or switch the panel off and on, which does the same.

## The devices

| Device | Topic |
| --- | --- |
| Seed sensor | [Configure a seed sensor](configure-seed-sensor.md) |
| Pressure sensor | [Configure a pressure sensor](configure-pressure-sensor.md) |
| HUB8 input device | [Configure a HUB8](configure-hub8.md) |
| Tramline actuator controller | [Configure a tramline actuator controller](configure-tramline-actuator.md) |
| Electric motor controllers — their own way in | [Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md) |


# Configure a seed sensor

For a seed sensor the new address is simply **the number of the row** — the same number the operator sees under the column on the home screen. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this sensor on the cable, **“Agronomist”** level.

The address of a seed sensor can only be changed while the sensor is **working normally**. A tube sensor is ready as soon as it is connected. An **open** sensor must sit on its bracket, or be held so that **no daylight falls into the optical channel** — the gap between the two glasses. In direct light the sensor reports a permanent seed flow and does not accept the new address.

::: steps
1. Choose **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”** → **“Seed sensor”** and press **“MENU”**. The menu has three items.

   ![The “Seed sensor” configuration menu.](figures/konf-seed)

2. Leave **“Sensor address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. Select **“New address”** and set the row number with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**.

4. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”**. The panel answers **“Done”**.

   ![The panel confirms with “Done”.](figures/info-done)

5. Disconnect the sensor and connect it again. On the home screen, check that it appears under its row.
:::

When all sensors are done, set the level back to **“Operator”**, or switch the panel off and on.


# Configure a pressure sensor

Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this sensor on the cable, **“Agronomist”** level. The menu has the same three items as every configuration menu. The address values are not printed in this manual: **take them from the data sheet of the system.**

::: steps
1. Choose **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”** → **“Pressure sensor”** and press **“MENU”**. The menu shows **“Sensor address”**, **“New address”** and **“Set”**.

2. Leave **“Sensor address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. Select **“New address”**. The panel proposes the correct value for the first pressure sensor by itself; each further sensor takes the next one. Check the value against the data sheet and correct it with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** if needed.

4. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”**. The panel answers **“Done”**.

5. Disconnect the sensor and connect it again. On the home screen, check that its indicator appears.
:::

When all sensors are done, set the level back to **“Operator”**, or switch the panel off and on. Its parameters: [Pressure sensor](pressure-sensor.md).


# Configure a HUB8

The HUB8 carries several sensors at once. Its menu is longer than the others: after the device address come its **eight channels**, each with a type and a number. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this HUB8 on the cable, **“Agronomist”** level.

::: {.anatomy fig="konf-hub8"}
1. **“Device address”** — which HUB8 the menu talks to. Leave it at **“AUTO”**.
2. **“Channel 1 type”** — what kind of sensor is wired to channel 1.
3. **“Channel 1 address”** — which sensor of that kind it is: hopper 1, dispenser 2, and so on.
4. **The value** of the selected item, changed with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**.
5. **Scroll bar.** Channels 2 to 8 follow in the same pairs, then **“Set”**.

The HUB8 menu with its first channels.
:::

The type and the number together make the sensor appear on the home screen under the right icon.

::: steps
1. Choose **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”** → **“HUB8”** and press **“MENU”**.

2. Leave **“Device address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. For each channel that carries a sensor, set **“Channel N type”** and **“Channel N address”** with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**. Leave a channel that carries nothing as it is.

4. Select **“Set”** at the end of the menu and press **“MENU”**. The panel answers **“Done”**.

5. Disconnect the HUB8 and connect it again. On the home screen, check that each sensor appears under its icon.
:::

When all devices are done, set the level back to **“Operator”**, or switch the panel off and on.


# Configure a tramline actuator controller

The actuator controller carries three things at once — the tramline actuator and the two marker sensors of the bout — and each has its own line. That is why one controller serves an actuator and both markers. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this controller on the cable, **“Agronomist”** level.

::: {.anatomy fig="konf-act"}
