1. **“Device address”** — which controller the menu talks to. Leave it at **“AUTO”**.
2. **“Actuator”** — the number of the tramline actuator this controller drives, or **“No”** if it drives none.
3. **“Input device, channel 1”** — the first marker sensor, or **“No”**.
4. **“Input device, channel 2”** — the second marker sensor, or **“No”**.
5. **“Set”** — writes the three lines to the controller.

The configuration menu of a tramline actuator controller, all lines still at **“No”**.
:::

::: steps
1. Choose **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”** → **“Tramline actuator”** and press **“MENU”**.

2. Leave **“Device address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. Set **“Actuator”**, **“Input device, channel 1”** and **“Input device, channel 2”** with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**.

4. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”**. The panel answers **“Done”**.

5. Disconnect the controller and connect it again. On the home screen, check that the actuator and the markers appear.
:::

When all devices are done, set the level back to **“Operator”**, or switch the panel off and on. The actuator's own settings: [Tramline actuator](tramline-actuator.md); the markers: [Marker sensors](marker-sensors.md).


# Configure the motor controllers

The controllers that drive the metering motors are not addressed from **“Sensors Configuration”**. They have their own way in, their own choice of controller kind and their own parameters.

> **WARNING**
>
> **For authorised service engineers.** As with every device on the cable: **one controller connected at a time.** The panel writes to whichever controller answers; with two of them connected, which one takes the new address is not defined.

## Open the motor controller menu

::: steps
1. Raise the level to **“Service”** ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md) — choose **“Service”**).

2. Press **“MENU”** → **“Service”** → **“Electric motors”**. The Motors screen opens.

   ![The Motors screen of motor 1, page “Registers”.](figures/motors-registers)

3. Press **“MENU”** on the Motors screen. Two items appear, both at the **“Agronomist”** level: **“Change address”** and **“Configuration”**.

   ![The menu of the Motors screen.](figures/motors-menu)
:::

On a panel built for a system without electric motors, **“Electric motors”** is not in the **“Service”** menu at all.

## Change the address

::: steps
1. Select **“Change address”** and press **“MENU”**. Three items open.

2. **“Motor address”** — the address the controller answers on now. Leave it as found.

3. **“New address”** — the address it is to take. **Take it from the data sheet of the system; the values are not printed in this manual.**

4. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”** to write it.
:::

## Choose the controller kind

**“Configuration”** opens the configuration of the controller. Four kinds are supported, offered by number:

| Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **“1)universal”** | The universal controller: two DC channels or one stepper channel on the same board. |
| **“2)DC motor”** | A DC motor controller. |
| **“3)STEPPER fw0.006+”** | A stepper controller, firmware 0.006 and later. |
| **“4)BGxxCI”** | A BG45CI motor with the controller built in, on the older board. |

The panel reads the kind back from the controller and opens on the one that answers. Choosing another kind by hand is how a replacement board is set up — not a way to change what a motor is.

## Set the parameters

Every configuration menu ends with **“Set”**, and **“Set”** carries a value of its own: the **address group**, 0 to 3. **Nothing reaches the controller until “Set” is entered** — the items above it change the numbers the panel holds, not those the controller runs on.

| Kind | What it is given |
| --- | --- |
| STEPPER | **“Pulses”** 1 … 8192 — the pulses of one turn of the motor shaft; **“Motor type”** from a list; **“Set”**. |
| BGxxCI | **“Pulses”** 1 … 8192; **“Set”**. Nothing else — the controller carries the rest. |
| DC motor | **“Pulses”**, **“Motor type”**, the regulator terms **“PID kP”**, **“PID kI”**, **“PID kD”** (0 … 65535, read as hundredths), **“TURBINA”** 0/1, and two speed–time pairs **“TIME1”** / **“SPEED1”**, **“TIME2”** / **“SPEED2”**; **“Set”**. |
| universal | The largest set, in three menus: **“Work mode”**, **“Inputs setup”** and **“Parameters”**. |

The **“Parameters”** menu of the universal controller:

| Parameter | Range |
| --- | --- |
| **“Motor type”** | 0 … 255, from the controller's own table |
| **“Pulses”** | 1 … 8192 per shaft turn |
| **“Acceleration,Ms”** / **“Deceleration,Ms”** | 50 … 65535 — the ramp up and down |
| **“Minimum, rpm”** / **“Maximum, rpm”** | 0 … 65535 — the shaft speed window |
| **“PID kP”**, **“PID kI”**, **“PID kD”** | 0 … 65535, hundredths |
| **“!! Temp,\*C”** | 0 … 200 — the temperature at which the controller alarms |
| **“I_peak,A”** / **“I_peak,mS”** | the peak current and how long it may be drawn |
| **“I_push,A”** / **“I_push,Sec”** | the breakaway current and its time |
| **“I_hilo,A”** / **“I_hilo,Sec”** | the sustained-current threshold and its time |
| **“Set”** | writes all of it, at the chosen address group |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The current and temperature limits protect the motor.** They are the controller's own protection thresholds: set them from the data sheet of the motor, not by trying values until the alarms stop.

The items **“PID kP”**, **“PID kI”**, **“PID kD”**, **“TURBINA”**, **“TIME1”**, **“SPEED1”**, **“TIME2”**, **“SPEED2”**, **“!! Temp,\*C”**, **“I_peak,A”**, **“I_push,A”**, **“I_hilo,A”** and their time partners read the same in every language of the panel.

Reading what the controller reports: [Motor controller diagnostics](motor-controller-diagnostics.md).


# Motor controller diagnostics

The Motors screen is also the diagnostic screen of a motor controller. It shows, live, what the controller reports about itself. Open it with **“MENU”** → **“Service”** → **“Electric motors”** (**“Service”** level). The working view of the same screen is described in [Motors screen](motors-screen.md).

::: {.anatomy fig="motors-registers"}
1. **“Motor #1”** — which motor is shown. **(−)** / **(+)** step to the previous / next motor.
2. **“Registers”** — the name of the page.
3. **The status word** — sixteen bits of the controller; a lit (yellow) cell is a bit that is set.
4. **The legend of the bits** — the number and the name of each bit. [Table below](#the-status-bits).
5. **“Speed”** / **“Target speed”** — what the shaft is doing against what the panel asked for. A gap that does not close is the first sign of a load the motor cannot carry.
6. **“Error code”** / **“Act.posit.”** — the controller's own error number ([codes](motor-fault-codes.md)), and the position it counts itself at.
7. **“Volt.mot.,mV”** / **“Volt.elec.,mV”** — the voltage at the motor and at the electronics, in millivolts. A motor voltage far below the electronics voltage means the supply sags under load.
8. **“Temperat.,C”** / **“Current,mA”** — the controller's temperature and the current it draws. Compare the current with **“I_hilo,A”** set for this motor ([Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md)).

The **“Registers”** page of motor 1, standing.
:::

## The status bits

| Bit | Name | Bit | Name |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Enable | 8 | Toggle |
| 1 | Error | 9 | CmdTgl |
| 2 | Warn. | 10 | CmdErr |
| 3 | Moving | 11 | StpHalt |
| 4 | Reach | 12 | LimCur |
| 5 | Limit | 13 | LimVel |
| 6 | FolErr | 14 | LimPos |
| 7 | HomDone | 15 | LimSVel |

The legend is drawn in English on every panel, whatever its language: it is a bit map of the controller, not a message to the operator.

## The fault counters

![The statistics page of motor 1 on field 1.](figures/motors-statistics)

The faults this motor has collected **on the chosen field** — they are part of the field statistics, not of the motor:

| Counter | What it counts |
| --- | --- |
| **“Jammed”** | The rotor stalled and the controller had to give up or back off. |
| **“Disconnects”** | The controller stopped answering. |
| **“Other”** | Everything else the controller reported, overcurrent and overtemperature included — they have no counter of their own. |
| **“In failure”** | The distance in metres this motor spent in a fault state. |

Each counter is **white at zero and red once it is not**. A red figure does not mean the motor is faulty now — it means it was, somewhere on this field, and the seed placed there is worth a look.


# The Service menu

**“MENU”** → **“Service”**. Which items you see depends on the access level ([Access levels](access-levels.md)). The panel has four levels — **“Operator”**, **“Agronomist”**, **“Service”** and **“Debug”**; **“Debug”** sits above **“Service”** and is used at manufacture only.

![The “Service” menu, top part.](figures/menu-service)

| Item | Level | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Profile”** | Service | Which devices the machine has, and how many. [The profile](profile.md) |
| **“Sensors Configuration”** | Agronomist | Giving devices their address. [Device configuration](device-configuration.md) |
| **“Registers”** | Debug | A raw register view. Not part of any procedure. |
| **“Electric motors”** | Service | The metering motor controllers. [Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md) |
| **“Serial number”** | Debug | The serial number of the panel, entered once at manufacture. |
| **“Count seeds always”** | Agronomist | **“No”** / **“Yes”** — keep the seed counter running even when the panel would otherwise stop it. |
| **“Enter key”** | Agronomist | Enters the licence key that takes the panel out of the demonstration state. |
| **“Set trial”** | Service | Starts the demonstration period. |
| **“Trial, hours”** | Service | 1 … 999 — how long that period lasts. |
| **“Imitation mode”** | Service | **“No”** / **“Yes”** — the panel works from simulated data. See the warning below. |
| **“Display type”** | Debug | Which display the firmware drives. Set at manufacture. |
| **“Launch updater”** | Service | Restarts the panel into the updater to take firmware from the memory card. |

Three further items — the tracker protocol and two switches for logging to the memory card — exist in the firmware but are set never to be shown. They cannot be reached at any level.

> **WARNING**
>
> **“Imitation mode” is not a test aid to be left on.** With it on, the panel works from figures it makes up: every number on every screen and every entry in the statistics is invented. Switch it off before the machine goes to work — and check it if a panel reports a plausible field it never sowed.

**“Imitation mode”**, **“Display type”**, **“Launch updater”** and the two logging switches are shown in English whatever language the panel is set to.


# How alarms work

An alarm is a window that opens over the working screen, with a warning tone. It tells you that one device — a sensor, an actuator, a motor controller — or the system as a whole has found a fault. The alarm topics in this section are grouped by the device that raises the alarm. **Look for the words you see on the screen**, not for a description of them.

## When the panel raises an alarm

A fault is not reported the moment it appears. **The condition must hold without a break for the time set in “Alarm delay” before the alarm window opens.**

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Where it is set | **“Settings”** menu, item **“Alarm delay”**. Available at the **“Operator”** access level. See [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md). |
| Range | **2 to 20 seconds**, in steps of 1 second. |
| Default | **3 seconds.** A value outside the range is reset to the default by itself. |

A short delay makes the panel react quickly, but also to brief disturbances — a single bump, a momentary gap in the seed flow. A long delay keeps the screen quiet, but a real fault can run for up to twenty seconds before you are told.

> **TIP**
>
> **If the system alarms too often on a rough field, raise “Alarm delay” first.** Change the sensor settings only when a longer delay does not help.

Two cases do not follow the delay:

- **Lost communication** is counted in polls, not in seconds. **“Connection lost”** appears after **three polls in a row** without an answer from the device.
- **Right after a sensor has been set up**, its alarms are not processed for a short blocking period. This prevents a burst of alarms while a device is being configured.

## The alarm window

::: {.anatomy fig="alarm-window"}
1. **“FAILURE!”** — the title of every alarm window, whatever the fault. It is not the fault itself.
2. **The alarm text** — the fault. Look it up under this text in the alarm topics.
3. **The kind of device** that raises the alarm — here a hopper sensor. The same text can come from different devices; this line tells you which.
4. **The number of the device** — here hopper 2. When several devices of the same kind raise the same alarm, they share one window and are listed together, for example **#3-5,8**.
5. **“Close”** — closes this alarm. [Below](#closing-an-alarm).

The alarm window of an empty hopper.
:::

The alarms of the panel itself carry the line **“HOME - close message”** in their text instead of a device line. The alarms of the sensors do not.

## Closing an alarm

| What you do | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Touch the red **“Close”** button in the window, or press **“HOME”** | This alarm closes. If more alarms are waiting, the next one opens. While the window is open, **“HOME”** is the only lit button. |
| Hold **“HOME”** | Every open alarm window closes at once and the panel returns to the home screen. |

Closing a window does not repair the fault. The alarms of a sensor that are still active are listed on its status screen — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

## Alarms are hidden at the higher access levels

At the **“Agronomist”** and **“Service”** levels alarm windows are not shown. They are not lost: they wait. When you return to **“Operator”**, the panel drops the ones that have gone away and shows the ones that are still true, one after another. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).

## Not alarms: SLOWER and FASTER

When the travel speed leaves the permitted range, no alarm window opens. The home screen shows **“SLOWER”** or **“FASTER”** instead, and keeps showing it while you correct the speed. See [Indicators](indicators.md).

## How the alarm topics are written

Every alarm has its own heading with the text exactly as on the screen; where the message has two lines on the panel, both lines are given. Under it: what the panel has detected, and what to check, in the order a mechanic checks it — the quick checks on the panel first, then the machine, then the sensor itself.

> **NOTE**
>
> If the checks do not clear the fault, call the service support. The contact details are on the back cover of the printed manual.


# Any device: connection lost or wrong device type

These two alarms are not tied to one kind of device. The name of the device in the alarm window tells you which one is affected. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Connection lost”

**What it means.** The panel has received no answer from the device in three polls in a row. This applies to sensors, actuators, controllers and the input device alike.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The device is connected to the network.
2. The cable and the connector of the device.
3. The power supply of the device. It must meet the values in the device passport.

## “Wrong device type!”

**What it means.** A device of another kind answers where the panel expects a device of this kind. The cause is either a wrong setting in the system profile or a wrong configuration of the device itself.

**What to do:** call the service support. Do not try to correct it by changing the profile or the device configuration at random — see [Device configuration](device-configuration.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> The status screen of a sensor shows the same two states as **“No connection”** and **“Wrong device type!”** in red — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).


# Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms

The fan sensor and the dispenser shaft sensor use the same two messages. **The device name in the alarm window tells you which one it is.** How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Low speed of rotation” / “High speed of rotation”

**What it means.** The fan or the dispenser shaft turns slower or faster than allowed.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The component being watched — the fan or the dispenser and its drive.
2. The settings of the sensor: for the fan **“Minimum, rpm”**, **“Maximum, rpm”** and **“Pulses”** — see [Fan sensor](fan-sensor.md); for the dispenser — see [Dispenser sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
3. **Dispenser only:** the travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
4. The sensor itself is serviceable.
5. **Dispenser only:** run the calibration — see [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md).

## “No rotation”

**What it means.** The dispenser shaft does not turn. Only the dispenser shaft sensor raises this alarm.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The dispenser and its drive.
2. The settings of the sensor — see [Dispenser sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
3. The sensor itself is serviceable.


# Hopper empty

The hopper sensor sits in the hopper at a fixed height. It reports when the product falls below it. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Hopper empty”

**What it means.** The level of the product in the hopper is very low. The hopper needs refilling.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Fill the hopper.
2. If the product stands above the height at which the sensor is mounted and the alarm stays, check that the sensor is serviceable. Its status screen shows the level on its input as **“0”** or **“1”** — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).

The hopper sensor has no settings of its own beyond the common ones — see [Hopper, implement position and engine sensors](hopper-position-engine-sensors.md).


# Air pressure too high or too low

The pressure sensor measures the positive pressure or the vacuum of the air system. Both alarms look at the absolute value — the size of the pressure or vacuum, whichever it is. The sensor's limits are described in [Pressure sensor](pressure-sensor.md). How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “High pressure”

**What it means.** The measured pressure or vacuum is greater than allowed.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Reduce the speed of the fan or turbine.
2. The position of the regulating damper of the air intake, if there is one.
3. The tube to the pressure sensor is connected correctly, and the measuring line is free of blockages.

## “Low pressure”

**What it means.** The measured pressure or vacuum is less than allowed.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Increase the speed of the fan or turbine.
2. The position of the regulating damper of the air intake, if there is one.
3. The air duct for leaks.
4. The tube to the pressure sensor is connected correctly, and the measuring line is free of blockages.

> **NOTE**
>
> The liquid fertilizer pump controller has its own **“High pressure”** alarm for the liquid line. It is a different alarm — see [Liquid fertilizer pump](alarms-pump-controller.md).


# Application rate too low, too high, or not under control

The section sensors — seed, dry fertilizer and liquid fertilizer — compare the rate they measure with the target. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

> **TIP**
>
> **Check the travel speed first.** Every rate on the panel is worked out from the distance travelled. If the speed on the screen is wrong, every rate is wrong by the same amount, and the sensors are not to blame.

## “Not under control!” / “Check seeding rate”

**What it means.** Over the set number of section sensors, the rate of the product is below the minimum needed for the panel to start controlling the application at all.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. The target rate, or the minimum alarm rate — which one depends on the control mode of the group of sections.
3. There is enough product in the hoppers or in the tank.
4. Seed or dry fertilizer sensor: **“Fraction”** in its settings. The value may have to be **reduced**. See [Seed and fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md).
5. Liquid fertilizer sensor: **“Pulses per liter”** in its settings. The value may have to be **reduced**. See [Liquid fertilizer](liquid-fertilizer.md).
6. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

## “Under allowable rate”

**What it means.** A section sensor — seed, dry fertilizer or liquid fertilizer — has measured too little product during work.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. There is enough product in the hoppers or in the tank.
2. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
3. Seed or dry fertilizer sensor: **“Fraction”**. The value may have to be **reduced**.
4. Liquid fertilizer sensor: **“Pulses per liter”**. The value may have to be **reduced**.
5. Seed sensor: its status on the status screen (**“Information”** in its context menu) — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).
6. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

## “Over allowable rate”

**What it means.** A section sensor — seed, dry fertilizer or liquid fertilizer — has measured too much product during work.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. Seed or dry fertilizer sensor: **“Fraction”**. The value may have to be **increased**.
3. Liquid fertilizer sensor: **“Pulses per liter”**. The value may have to be **increased**.
4. Seed sensor: its status on the status screen.
5. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> How far the rate may stand from the target before these alarms is set by **“Rate error,%”** of the sensor group — [Seed and fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md), [Liquid fertilizer](liquid-fertilizer.md). Columns under the control line on the home screen are not guarded — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).


# Too many doubles or skips

Doubles and skips are counted only in the **“Precise”** mode of seeding — on a precision planter. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “High % of doubles”

**What it means.** The share of doubles the sensor counts is higher than the set limit.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. **“Doubles error,%”** in the settings of the seed sensor — is the limit sensible? See [Seed and fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md).
3. **“Fraction”** in the settings of the seed sensor. The value may have to be **increased**.
4. The sensor's status on its status screen — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).
5. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

## “High % of skips”

**What it means.** The share of skips the sensor counts is higher than the set limit.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. There is enough seed in the hoppers.
3. **“Skips error,%”** in the settings of the seed sensor — is the limit sensible?
4. **“Fraction”** in the settings of the seed sensor. The value may have to be **reduced**.
5. The sensor's status on its status screen.
6. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?



# Tramline: actuator stalled or product in the tramline

The tramline actuator shuts the sections of the tramline bout. Two gate position sensors tell the panel where its shutter stands. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Stall”

**What it means.** The tramline actuator has jammed.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The gate position sensors of the actuator are serviceable.
2. The mechanism of the tramline actuator is serviceable.

## “Illegal state”

**What it means.** Both gate position sensors have been triggered at the same time. With a serviceable installation this cannot happen.

**What to check:** the gate position sensors are serviceable.

## “Seeding to tramline”

**What it means.** A section that should be shut off for the tramline still delivers too much product. The seed sensor, the dry fertilizer sensor or the liquid fertilizer sensor of that section has measured it in the tramline control mode.

**Seed sensor or dry fertilizer sensor — check, in this order:**

1. The metering unit and the flow cut-off mechanism are serviceable.
2. **“Tolerable sowing to tramline,%”** in the settings of the group of section sensors. The value may have to be **increased**. See [Seed and fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md).
3. **“Fraction”** in the settings of the group of the alarming sensor. The value may have to be **increased**.
4. The sensor's status on its status screen — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).

**Liquid fertilizer sensor — check, in this order:**

1. The metering unit and the flow cut-off mechanism are serviceable.
2. **“Tolerable leak to tramline,%”** in the settings of the group of section sensors. The value may have to be **increased**. See [Liquid fertilizer](liquid-fertilizer.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> Which sections belong to which actuator is set in **“Actuators to sensors mapping”** — [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md). The rhythm: [Tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).


# Seed or fertilizer sensor clogged, light-struck or broken

The seed and dry fertilizer sensors count the product optically: an emitter shines across the channel, a receiver sees each grain. These alarms report the state of the sensor itself, not the rate. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Clogged”

**What it means.** The seed or dry fertilizer sensor has detected that its optical channel is blocked.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Remove the blockage.
2. Check for a build-up of dust in the channel.
3. Check the power supply of the sensor. It must meet the values in the device passport.

## “Light struck”

**What it means.** The seed or fertilizer sensor has detected an extremely high level of light in its optical channel.

**What to do:** keep direct sunlight out of the optical channel of the sensor.

## “Broken”

**What it means.** The seed or dry fertilizer sensor has detected a fault of its own. It may have to be replaced.

**What to do:** check the power supply of the sensor. It must meet the values in the device passport. If the power supply is in order, the sensor may have to be replaced — call the service support.

## “Old firmware! Wrong S&D calc!”

**What it means.** A seed sensor with outdated firmware is in use. It counts, but its skips and doubles cannot be trusted.

**What to do:** call the service support to have the firmware of the sensor updated.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> The status screen of the sensor shows the same states — **“Clogged”**, **“Light struck”**, **“Faulty”** — in red: [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).


# Tractor engine: oil pressure, battery charge, fuel, air filter

All on-board engine sensors share one alarm text: **“FAILURE”**. **The name of the sensor above the text tells you which one has triggered.** How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md). The settings named below are described in [Hopper, implement position and engine sensors](hopper-position-engine-sensors.md).

## “Emergency oil pressure” — “FAILURE”

**What it means.** The low oil pressure sensor has triggered.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The low oil pressure sensor is serviceable.
2. **“Activation signal”** in the settings of the low oil pressure sensor.
3. If an ignition key sensor is in the profile: is its monitoring switched on?
4. If an ignition key sensor is in the profile: is it serviceable?

## “No battery charge” — “FAILURE”

**What it means.** The battery is not being charged.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The battery charge sensor is serviceable.
2. **“Activation signal”** in the settings of the battery charge sensor.
3. If an ignition key sensor is in the profile: is its monitoring switched on?
4. If an ignition key sensor is in the profile: is it serviceable?

## “Low fuel” — “FAILURE”

**What it means.** Little fuel is left in the tank.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The fuel level sensor is serviceable.
2. **“Activation signal”** in the settings of the fuel level sensor.
3. **“Signal delay, sec”** in the settings of the fuel level sensor. The default is **15 seconds**.

## “Air filter” — “FAILURE”

**What it means.** The air filter is clogged.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The air filter sensor is serviceable.
2. **“Activation signal”** in the settings of the air filter sensor.
3. **“Signal delay, sec”** in the settings of the air filter sensor. The default is **5 seconds**.



# Product rate by weight too low, too high, or impossible

These alarms are raised by the system as a whole, not by one device. They exist **for each of the four products** separately: the number in the message is the number of the product. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Rate of Product 1” / “is too low!” — or — “is too high!”

The same for Product 2, 3 and 4.

**What it means.** The product is applied below or above its target rate in kilograms per hectare.

**Product metered by an electric motor — check, in this order:**

1. The target rate of the product.
2. The speed limits in force, on the status screen of the speed sensor — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).
3. The settings of the electric motor that drives the dispenser shaft — see [Dispenser electric motor](dispenser-motor.md).
4. The metering unit.
5. The rotation sensor of the electric motor is serviceable.
6. The working load of the motor. **Below 20 % or above 80 %**, try a metering roller of another size: a **larger** one if too little is applied, a **smaller** one if too much.
7. Calibrate the metering roller — see [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).

**Dispenser sensor with “Weight control” switched on — check, in this order:**

1. The target rate of the product.
2. The settings of the dispenser shaft rotation sensor — see [Dispenser sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
3. The metering unit.
4. The dispenser sensor is serviceable.
5. Calibrate the metering roller — see [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md).

## “Product dosage is” / “impossible! Check product” / “rate and calibration!”

**What it means.** With the current settings and target rate, the product cannot be applied by weight at all.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The target rate of the product.
2. **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** of the speed sensor — see [Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).
3. The settings of the electric motors that apply the products by weight, above all **“Minimum, rpm”** and **“Maximum, rpm”**.
4. Calibrate the metering rollers of the electric motors.
5. If that does not help: fit metering rollers of another size.

> **TIP**
>
> The calibration screen of a metering motor shows the speed window the current roller allows. If it reads **“Can not provide dosage!”**, no calibration will help — the roller does not suit the rate. See [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).


# User is Agronomist: alarms will not be shown

How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “User is Agronomist!” / “Alarms will not be shown!”

**What it means.** The conditions for controlling the product application are met — the machine is working — while the **“Agronomist”** access level is active. At this level the panel does not show alarm windows. The message appears **only once** for the whole time you work at this level.

**What to do:** set the access level back to **“Operator”**:

::: steps
1. Press **“MENU”** on the home screen and select **“Settings”**.

2. Select **“User”** and choose **“Operator”** with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**.

3. Press **“MENU”**. Going down a level needs no PIN.
:::

Switching the panel off and on does the same: after every power-on the panel starts at **“Operator”**.

> **NOTE**
>
> **Expect a short run of alarms on the way back.** The alarms raised while the level was high have waited. The panel drops those that have gone away and shows the ones that are still true. It is the backlog, not a new fault. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).


# Travel speed sensor failed, or speed limits contradict

How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Speed sensor #1 failed” / “Speed sensor #2 failed”

**What it means.** The profile says the machine has **two** travel speed sensors, but the panel sees movement from only one of them. The number names the silent sensor. This alarm cannot appear on a machine with one speed sensor.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Check that both speed sensors are serviceable, and repair what you find.
2. If one sensor cannot be repaired now: change the system profile so that only one speed sensor is used — see [The profile](profile.md).

## “Error in settings of Min/Max”

**What it means.** The minimum and the maximum travel speed set for the speed sensor contradict each other. The panel cannot decide whether the current speed is allowed.

**What to do:** check **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** in the settings of the speed sensor. The minimum must be below the maximum. See [Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).

> **NOTE**
>
> **“SLOWER” and “FASTER” are not alarms.** When the speed leaves the permitted range, no alarm window opens: the home screen shows **“SLOWER”** or **“FASTER”** and keeps showing it while you correct the speed. See [Indicators](indicators.md).


# Metering motor: jammed, electrical faults, bootloader

These alarms come from the controller that drives an electric motor of a dispenser. The name in the alarm window tells you which motor. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Motor jammed!”

**What it means.** The controller does not see rotation while the motor should be running.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The metering unit is serviceable and turns freely.
2. The rotation sensor of the motor is serviceable, and so is its connection to the controller — the cable and the connector.

## “Short circuit”

**What it means.** The controller has detected a short circuit.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The cable connection: the cables and the connector are intact.
2. Replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “Over current”

**What it means.** The current has gone above the limit.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The motor and the seeding mechanism for jamming.
2. The cable connection: the cables and the connector are intact.
3. Replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “Under voltage”

**What it means.** The supply voltage of the motor is below the allowed value. The motor cannot run.

**Measure the supply voltage first.**

**If it is too low:**

1. The alternator is serviceable.
2. The tension of the alternator belts.
3. The power harness is connected firmly to the battery or the alternator terminals, as the required supply voltage demands.
4. The cable connections make reliable electrical contact.

**If the supply voltage is in order:** replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “Over voltage”

**What it means.** The supply voltage of the motor is above the allowed value. The motor cannot run.

**Measure the supply voltage first.**

**If it is too high:**

1. The alternator is serviceable.
2. The power harness is connected firmly to the battery or the alternator terminals, as the required supply voltage demands.
3. The cable connections make reliable electrical contact.

**If the supply voltage is in order:** replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “Over temperature”

**What it means.** The motor has overheated.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Let the motor cool down.
2. Replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “FAILURE”

**What it means.** The controller has detected an unusual fault that needs the service support.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Read the fault code: context menu of the motor → **“Information”** → line **“Last fault”**. See [Read the motor fault code](motor-fault-codes.md).
2. Replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.
3. Give the code and the number of the motor to the service support.

## “Device in bootloader!”

**What it means.** The controller has stayed in its firmware update mode and is not running its working program. It cannot drive the motor.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Switch the power off and on.
2. If the message returns, the firmware update of the controller was not completed. Call the service support.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> The liquid fertilizer pump controller raises the same electrical alarms — [Liquid fertilizer pump](alarms-pump-controller.md).


# Liquid fertilizer pump: pressure and rate alarms

The pump controller is built on the same electronics as the controller of a metering motor. Besides the alarms on this page it raises **all the electrical alarms of the metering motor controller** — **“Short circuit”**, **“Over current”**, **“Under voltage”**, **“Over voltage”**, **“Over temperature”**, **“FAILURE”** and **“Device in bootloader!”** — with the same meaning and the same actions: see [Metering motor alarms](alarms-motor-controller.md). How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “High pressure”

**What it means.** The measured liquid pressure is greater than allowed.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Reduce the travel speed.
2. In the settings of the pump controller, increase **“Max pressure, Bar”** — see [Liquid fertilizer](liquid-fertilizer.md).

## “Pressure sensor failure!”

**What it means.** The signal from the pressure sensor has gone well outside its 4–20 mA working range.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The connection of the sensor to the controller — the cable and the connector are intact.
2. The sensor is serviceable. If it has failed, replace it.

The status screen of the pump controller shows the pressure and the raw sensor signal in mA — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).

## “Rate low”

**What it means.** The pump controller cannot reach the set rate.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed and is reasonably steady.
2. The working load of the pump. **Above 90 %:** drive more slowly.
3. **Load under 90 %, or jumping strongly:** increase **“Product rate error,%”** in the **“Settings”** menu — see [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md).
4. The pump is serviceable.

## “Rate high”

**What it means.** The pump controller applies more than the set rate.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed and is reasonably steady.
2. The working load of the pump. **Under 10 %:** drive faster.
3. **Load above 10 %, or jumping strongly:** increase **“Product rate error,%”** in the **“Settings”** menu.
4. The pump is serviceable.


# Read the fault code of an electric motor

When a metering motor raises **“FAILURE”**, its controller also records a numeric code. Read it out and give it to the service support together with the number of the motor.

::: steps
1. On the home screen, open the context menu of the faulty motor: hold its tile, or hold **“MENU”**, step to the motor with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and press **“MENU”**.

2. Select **“Information”** and press **“MENU”**. The status screen of the motor opens.

3. Read the line **“Last fault”**. The status of the motor reads **“Faulty”** while any of its alarms is active.
:::

The same code is shown as **“Error code”** on the Motors screen — see [Motors screen](motors-screen.md) and [Motor controller diagnostics](motor-controller-diagnostics.md).

## The codes

The panel shows only the number. The descriptions come from the motor controller itself.

### Command and parameter errors

The controller refused something the panel asked of it.

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| -250 | Invalid command |
| -251 | Unexpected command |
| -252 | Invalid command syntax |
| -253 | Invalid command arguments |
| -260 | Invalid number of arguments |
| -261 | Specified index is greater than FFFFh |
| -262 | Specified sub-index is greater than FFh |
| -300 | Parameter does not exist |
| -301 | Memory write operation failed |
| -302 | Restore operation failed |
| -306 | Parameter cannot be written |
| -307 | Parameter cannot be read |
| -308 | Parameter value out of range |
| -316 | Version of the stored parameter set does not match the firmware version |
| -318 | Stored parameter set has an invalid check sum |
| -322 | Parameter cannot be set: the axis is in motion |
| -325 | Parameter cannot be set: the positioning mode is inactive |
| -340 | Parameter cannot be set: a limit switch is active |
| -343 | Parameter cannot be set: a stop or halt command is being executed |
| -350 | Parameter not contained in the specified index |
| -351 | Parameter not contained in the specified sub-index |

### Device errors

The controller or the motor itself is in trouble.

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| -1000 | Low supply voltage |
| -1001 | Excessive supply voltage |
| -1002 | Low electronics supply voltage |
| -1003 | Excessive electronics supply voltage |
| -1020 | Overtemperature of the device |
| -1021 | Overtemperature of the heat sink |
| -1060 | Short circuit of a motor lead: between motor leads, motor and ground, or motor and power supply |
| -1061 | Motor overcurrent |
| -4000 | Following-difference error in the motion sequence |
| -5100 | Limit switch active |


# Buttons and gestures on every screen

![The seven buttons, left to right: HOME, MINUS, UP, MENU, DOWN, PLUS, BACK.](figures/buttons/row)

The panel lights only the buttons that do something on the screen in front of you. A dark button does nothing there. Where the buttons are: [The panel and its seven buttons](front-panel.md).

## Kinds of press and touch

| **Press or gesture** | **How** |
| --- | --- |
| Short press | Press a button and release. |
| Long press (hold) | Hold the button until the panel reacts. Some buttons do something else when held. |
| Touch and hold | Keep a finger on one spot of the screen until the panel reacts. |
| Double tap | Two quick taps with one finger. |
| Two-finger tap | One tap with two fingers at once. |
| Swipe | A long movement of one finger across the screen. A short one is not recognised. |
| Two-finger swipe | The same with two fingers. |

## Home screen

| **Button or gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“HOME”** | Next working screen: the Table. |
| **“HOME”**, held | Locks or unlocks product application. One short beep confirms. |
| **“MENU”**, or two-finger tap | Opens the main menu. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | The first press selects a rate field (it blinks); the next ones raise or lower its target. |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Move to the previous or the next rate field. Nothing if the machine has only one. |
| **“BACK”** | Releases a blinking rate field; otherwise opens the tramline bout menu, if the tramline is on. |
| Double tap | Sets the alarm level from the rate being applied. Only while applying. |
| Touch and hold a device | Opens its context menu. |
| Touch and hold a rate field, then swipe up or down | Selects the field and changes its target. |
| Touch and hold a kg/ha indicator | Opens the number pad for that product's target rate. |
| Swipe left / right | Table / second home screen. |

## Second home screen

| **Button or gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“MENU”**, or touch the settings symbol | Opens the main menu. |
| **“HOME”**, or swipe left | Back to the home screen. |
| **“HOME”**, held, or touch and hold the hand | Locks or unlocks product application. |
| Touch and hold the rate, then swipe up or down | Changes the seeding rate. |
| Touch a red or green chevron | Takes a motor out of or into control. |
| Touch and hold a motor | Opens its context menu. |

## Table

| **Button** | **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Long two-finger swipe left or right | Next or previous table. |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Swipe up or down | Scroll the lines. |
| **“MENU”** | Two-finger tap | Asks **“Zero readings?”**. |
| **“HOME”** | Swipe left | Statistics. |
| **“BACK”** | Swipe right | Home screen. |

## Statistics

| **Button** | **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Swipe up or down | Scroll the report. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Two-finger swipe left or right | Show another field. |
| **“MENU”** | Two-finger tap | Menu of the screen. |
| **“HOME”** | Swipe left | Motors, or the home screen if there is none. |
| **“BACK”** | — | Home screen. |
| — | Swipe right | Table. |

## Motors

| **Button** | **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“HOME”** or **“BACK”** | Swipe left | Home screen. |
| — | Swipe right | Statistics. |
| — | Touch and hold a tile | Context menu of that motor. |

## In a menu

| **Button** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Move the selection up and down the list. |
| **“MENU”** | Enters the selected item. For a value in square brackets, opens the number pad. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Change the value of the selected item by one step. For a value in square brackets, they open the number pad. |
| **“BACK”** | Leaves the menu, one level up. |

## Number pad

| **Button or touch** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Touch the digits | Type the value. |
| Touch **“OK”**, or **“MENU”** (lit green) | Accept the value. |
| **“BACK”** (lit red), or touch outside the pad | Leave without changing anything. |
| Touch and hold the backspace | Clear the value. |
| Touch and hold **. −** | Switch the minus sign, where allowed. |

## Windows

| **Window** | **Buttons** |
| --- | --- |
| **Confirmation** | **“PLUS”** or touch **“Yes”** — confirm. **“MINUS”** or touch **“No”** — refuse. **“BACK”** — cancel. |
| **Information** | Closes by itself, or with a touch, **“PLUS”** or **“BACK”**. |
| **Alarm** | **“HOME”** or touch **“Close”** — close this alarm. **“HOME”** held — close and return to the home screen. The other buttons do nothing. |


# Terms

## Rates and control

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Rate** | The target intensity the operator sets. The panel compares the actual intensity against it and reports a deviation that is too large. |
| **Rate error** | How far the actual intensity may stand from the rate before that becomes an alarm. Set per sensor group, in per cent (**“Rate error,%”**). |
| **Product application control** | The panel does not judge the sowing at every moment: it starts watching once the conditions are met — the implement is lowered and moving. Until then a silent section is not a fault. |
| **Minimum alarm rate** | The lowest intensity still counted as normal — the control line of the diagram. Below it the section is reported, whatever the neighbours do. See [The section diagram](section-diagram.md). |
| **Path interval** | The stretch of the run over which skips, doubles and the other figures are gathered before they are redrawn. Set by **“Recalculation,m”**, which the panel renames **“Recalculation,sec”** when the seeding mode counts in seconds instead of metres. |
| **Manual lock** | Stopping all product application by hand, with a long press of **“HOME”**. A yellow hand on the home screen shows the lock is on. See [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md). |
| **Control (of a sensor)** | Whether the panel watches a sensor. A sensor out of control is shown with **!** and reports nothing. See [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md). |

## Seeding control modes

| **Mode** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Precise”** | Seeds per metre, with skips and doubles — row-crop planters. |
| **“Flow”** | Seeds per second against an alarm level — grain drills. |
| **“Hybrid”** | Seeds per metre, with a rate error as in “Precise”; the alarm level can be set automatically as in “Flow”. |

## Sensors

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Section control sensor** | The common name for a seed, dry fertilizer or liquid fertilizer sensor. One per section of the implement. |
| **Seed sensor** | Counts the seed passing one section. On a **row-crop planter** it also separates **doubles** and **skips**; on a grain drill it measures intensity only — the seeds arrive too close together to be told apart. |
| **Dry fertilizer sensor** | The same device, watching a granular fertilizer line. |
| **Liquid fertilizer sensor** | A flow meter counting the volume through one section. |
| **Speed sensor** | Measures the travel speed. Distance, area and every rate are calculated from it. |
| **Dispenser sensor** | Watches that the dispenser shaft turns. |
| **Fan sensor** | Watches the fan speed against a set minimum and maximum. |
| **Pressure sensor** | Watches positive pressure or vacuum, depending on how it is plumbed. |
| **Hopper sensor** | Reports when the product has fallen below the point where the sensor sits. |
| **Work position sensor** | Tells the panel whether the implement is lowered into work or raised for transport. |
| **Marker sensors** | Report which mechanical marker is down, so that the tramline bout can advance by itself. |

## Tramline

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Tramline** | A driving lane left unsown, made by shutting off one or several sections on chosen bouts. |
| **Rhythm** | The repeating sequence of bouts, with the bouts marked on which particular sections must not sow. See [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md). |
| **Bout** | One pass of the implement across the field. The rhythm counts them and returns to the first when it runs out. |
| **Tramline actuator** | The device that shuts the sections off. **One actuator controller carries three things:** the actuator itself and **both** marker sensors. |

## Devices

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **HUB8** (input device) | An eight-channel hub for sensors that have no controller of their own. It watches them and reports each to the panel as if it were a device. |
| **Electric motor controller** | Drives one or two dispenser motors, or the liquid fertilizer pump. Motors and pump share one controller design — which is why a machine cannot have a pump without also having the controller a motor would use. |
| **SCM** | Section Control Module — the interface through which a third-party navigation system can shut sections off. |
| **microSD** | The memory card, for reports, profiles and firmware updates. **FAT16 or FAT32** only. |
| **Profile** | The list of what the machine carries. The panel draws its screens from it. See [Profile](profile.md). |

## Access levels

| **Level** | **What it is for** |
| --- | --- |
| **Operator** | The level the panel starts at after every power-on. Everyday work. Only at this level are alarm windows shown. |
| **Agronomist** | The commissioning settings and resetting the statistics. Needs a **PIN**, which is different for every panel and is given in the device passport. |
| **Service** | The profile, the readdressing of devices, the “Reset to defaults” items. Used by the service department. |

Details: [Access levels](access-levels.md).


# Before you contact support

Most faults can be found with the manual. If you still need help, a complete message gets an answer faster.

## Check first

- The [check after installation](check-after-installation.md) was passed, or you know which step failed.
- You have looked up the text of the alarm in the alarm topics ([How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md)).
- The faulty device answers: **“Link:”** on its status screen ([The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md)), and the cable, the connector and the power supply are in order ([Any device: connection lost or wrong device type](alarms-any-device.md)).

## Write down

- The **exact text** of the alarm window, and the kind and number of the device named in it ([How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md)).
- The firmware version — where to read it: [Check after installation](check-after-installation.md), step 7.
- The machine and the number of rows.
- What was done before the fault appeared.
- The result of the check after installation, if you have recorded it.

## Take photos

- The sensor status screen of the faulty device ([The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md)).
- The alarm window.
- How the devices are connected.

## Whom to contact

1. **Your dealer or the partner who installed the system.** Start here.
2. **Agriwelt:** support@agriwelt.com. Attach the notes and the photos.
